text: EX-10.6 2 ex_1039554.htm EXHIBIT 10.6 ex_1039554.htm Exhibit 10.6 October 31, 2026 Reference is made to that certain Forbearance and Loan Modification Agreement (the “Agreement”), dated as of January 31, 2025, between the undersigned – Paid, Inc. (“Paid”) and Embolx, Inc. (“Embolx”). Pursuant to the Agreement, Paid agreed to forbear certain rights as described therein until the earlier of a Forbearance Termination Event set forth in Section 5 of the Agreement or September 30, 2025, which date was previously extended to August 30, 2026 pursuant to that certain letter agreement dated January 31, 2025 between Paid and Embolx (the “First Side Letter”), and further extended to October 31, 2026 pursuant to that certain letter agreement dated August 28, 2026 between Paid and Embolx (the “Second Side Letter,” and together with the First Side Letter, the “Prior Side Letters,” and such forbearance termination date, as extended thereby, the “Forbearance Date”). Paid hereby agrees to further extend the Forbearance Date under the Agreement, as previously extended by the Prior Side Letters, to January 31, 2027. Until the Forbearance Date, as extended hereby, Embolx shall notify Paid in writing within five (5) business days after Embolx receives a bona fide written offer from a third party to acquire Embolx, whether by merger, stock purchase, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets; provided that Embolx shall not be required to disclose any information in violation of any confidentiality obligation owed to such third party, and any information so provided shall be held in confidence by Paid. Except as expressly modified by this letter agreement, the Agreement, the Prior Side Letters, and the Loan Documents remain in full force and effect, and Paid reserves and does not waive any of its rights thereunder. PAID, INC. By : /s/ W. Austin Lewis, IV Austin Lewis Its: Chief Executive Officer ACKNOWLEDGED AND AGREED: EMBOLX, INC. By: /s/ Michael Allen Michael Allen Its: Chief Executive Officer

title: Protagenic Therapeutics, Inc.\new
text: EX-10.1 2 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 PROMISSORY NOTE Principal Amount: $250,000 Dated: November 4, 2026 FOR VALUE RECEIVED , Protagenic Therapeutics, a Delaware corporation (the “ Borrower ”), promises to pay to the order of Patness LLC (“ Lender ”) the principal sum of Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($250,000) (the “ Principal ”), together with interest thereon as provided below, in lawful money of the United States of America. 1. Interest; Computation; Payment . Interest on the outstanding Principal shall accrue at a rate of one percent (1.0%) per annum, simple interest, calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed, and shall be payable on the Maturity Date; provided, that if all Obligations (as defined below) are paid in full prior to the date that is three hundred sixty-five (365) days after the date of this Note, all accrued but unpaid interest shall be forgiven and no interest shall be due or payable. 2. Maturity; Repayment Triggers . The unpaid Principal, together with all accrued but unpaid interest (if any) and all other amounts payable hereunder (collectively, the “ Obligations ”), shall be due and payable upon the earliest to occur of: (i) the closing of any equity capital raise of any type by the Borrower for gross cash proceeds of at least One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) (an “ Equity Financing ”), in which case the Obligations shall be due and payable upon such closing, and (ii) the date that is 180 days from the date of this Note (the “ Maturity Date ”). 3. Prepayment . Borrower may prepay the Obligations, in whole or in part, at any time and from time to time without premium or penalty. Any partial prepayment shall be applied first to reasonable out-of-pocket fees and expenses then due hereunder (if any), next to accrued but unpaid interest (if any), and then to outstanding Principal. 4. Payment Mechanics . All payments shall be made in lawful money of the United States of America by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated in writing by Lender, without setoff or counterclaim. If any payment would be due on a day that is not a Business Day, such payment shall be due on the next succeeding Business Day, and interest shall continue to accrue until the date of payment. 5. Events of Default . Each of the following shall constitute an “Event of Default”: (a) Borrower fails to pay any amount due under this Note within five (5) Business Days after the date due; (b) Borrower breaches any other material covenant in this Note and such breach remains uncured for ten (10) Business Days after written notice from Lender; (c) Borrower commences any case or proceeding under any law relating to bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization or relief of debtors, or makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors; or (d) any such case or proceeding is commenced against Borrower and is not dismissed within sixty (60) days. 6. Remedies; Acceleration . Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default specified in Section 5(a) or 5(b), Lender may, by written notice to Borrower, declare all Obligations immediately due and payable, whereupon such amounts shall become immediately due and payable without presentment, demand, protest or other notice of any kind, all of which are expressly waived. Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default specified in Sections 5(c) or 5(d), all Obligations shall automatically and immediately become due and payable without any action by Lender. 7. Waivers . Borrower and, to the extent applicable, any sureties, guarantors and endorsers, hereby waive presentment, demand, notice of nonpayment or dishonor, protest, notice of protest, notice of intent to accelerate, notice of acceleration, diligence in collection, and all other notices and demands to the fullest extent permitted by law. 8. Amendments and Waivers . No amendment, modification, or waiver of any provision of this Note shall be effective unless in writing and signed by Borrower and Lender. Any waiver shall be limited to the specific instance and purpose for which given and shall not be deemed a continuing waiver. 9. Successors and Assigns . This Note shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns. Borrower may not assign this Note or any of its rights or obligations hereunder without Lender’s prior written consent. Lender may assign this Note with Borrower’s prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed); provided, that no such consent shall be required for an assignment by Lender to an affiliate controlled by Lender or to Lender’s estate, heirs, or any trust or other entity for estate or tax planning purposes, in each case upon written notice to Borrower. 10. Governing Law; Jurisdiction; Waiver of Jury Trial . This Note and any claim or controversy arising out of or relating to it shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflicts of laws rules. Borrower and Lender irrevocably submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York, and waive any objection based on inconvenient forum. EACH OF BORROWER AND LENDER HEREBY KNOWINGLY, VOLUNTARILY, AND INTENTIONALLY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO A TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION OR PROCEEDING ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS NOTE TO THE FULLEST EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW. 11. Notices . All notices and other communications hereunder shall be in writing and shall be deemed given when delivered by hand or nationally recognized overnight courier, or when sent by email in portable document format (PDF), to the parties at their respective addresses or email addresses set forth below (or at such other address or email address as a party may designate by notice in accordance with this Section). 12. Severability . If any provision of this Note is held invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect to the fullest extent permitted by law. 13. Entire Agreement . This Note constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous understandings, agreements, representations and warranties, both written and oral, with respect to such subject matter. 14. Counterparts; Electronic Signatures . This Note may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of this Note, and any signatures hereon, by email (including PDF), facsimile, DocuSign or other electronic transmission, and the use of electronic signatures, shall be effective and deemed original to the fullest extent permitted by the federal Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act, the New York Electronic Signatures and Records Act, and other applicable law. 15. Costs of Collection . If this Note is placed in the hands of an attorney for collection following an Event of Default, Borrower shall pay Lender’s reasonable out-of-pocket costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees) incurred in enforcing this Note. 16. Lost, Stolen or Destroyed Note . Upon receipt of a customary lost instrument affidavit and indemnity reasonably satisfactory to Borrower, Borrower shall issue a replacement note in the same principal amount and on the same terms as this Note. 17. Usury Savings . It is the intent of the parties that the interest and other charges under this Note shall not exceed the maximum rate permitted by law. If any such interest or charge is determined to be in excess of such maximum, such excess shall be deemed a mistake and shall be canceled automatically or, if theretofore paid, shall be credited against the Obligations or refunded to Borrower. 18. Headings . Headings are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Note. [Signature page follows] IN WITNESS WHEREOF , the undersigned have executed this Promissory Note as of the date first written above. BORROWER: PROTAGENIC THERAPEUTICS, a Delaware corporation By: /s/ Garo H. Armen Name: Garo H. Armen Title: Executive Chairman Date: Borrower Notice Information: Address: Email: LENDER: Patness LCC Signature: /s/ Patrice McNicoll Date: Lender Notice Information: Address: Email:

title: Elme Communities
text: EX-10.2 3 tm2629090d1_ex10-2.htm EXHIBIT 10.2 Exhibit 10.2 CONSULTING AGREEMENT CONSULTING AGREEMENT (this “ Agreement ”) dated as of _______, 2026, between Elme Communities Liquidating Trust (the “ Trust ”) and [individual] (“ Consultant ”). WHEREAS, prior to the dissolution of Elme Communities, a Maryland real estate investment trust (the “ Company ”) and the transfer of all the Company’s remaining assets and liabilities to the Trust, on November 6, 2026, the Consultant served as the Executive Vice President and [ ____ ] of the Company; WHEREAS, given the Consultant’s previous position with the Company, the Trust desires Consultant to provide consulting services to the Trust, and Consultant is willing to serve the Trust in a consulting capacity, commencing on November 7, 2026 (the “ Effective Date ”) for the period and upon such other terms and conditions as set forth in this Agreement. NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the promises, mutual covenants and other good and valuable consideration set forth in this Agreement, the receipt and sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, Consultant and the Trust (the “ Parties ”) agree as follows: 1. Entire Agreement . Except as otherwise expressly provided herein, this Agreement is the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and contains all agreements, whether written, oral, express or implied, between the Parties relating thereto and supersedes and extinguishes all other agreements relating thereto, whether written, oral, express or implied, between the Parties. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing in this Agreement supersedes, modifies or limits Consultant’s obligations under the Agreement and Release of Claims between Consultant and the Company, dated as of November 2, 2026, including any continuing cooperation obligations thereunder, which obligations are hereby reaffirmed and shall remain in full force and effect in accordance with their terms. 2. Term . This Agreement shall be effective as of the Effective Date and shall continue until April 30, 2027, unless such term is extended by the mutual written agreement of both Parties. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Consultant’s services under this Agreement may be terminated earlier pursuant to the provisions of Section 7. The period of time from the Effective Date through the termination of Consultant’s services hereunder is herein referred to as the “ Term .” 3. Services; Time Commitment; Independent Contractor Status . (a) During the Term, Consultant shall render such consulting services as may be reasonably requested from time to time by the Trust to facilitate the transition and wind-down of matters within the scope of Consultant’s knowledge and expertise and which relate to the services performed by the Consultant for Elme Communities prior to the Effective Date (the “ Services ”). The Parties acknowledge and agree that Consultant’s fulfillment of obligations to the Trust will not require Consultant’s full business time. In the time that Consultant is not providing the Services to the Trust, Consultant may accept other employment or engagements and may participate in any other activities without obtaining the Trust’s approval thereof; provided , however , that such other employment, engagements, or activities do not violate this Agreement and do not materially interfere or conflict with Consultant’s ability or commitment to perform the Services. The Trust will reasonably cooperate with Consultant to schedule the Services in a manner that accommodates Consultant’s other professional commitments. (b) Consultant acknowledges that (i) Consultant is an independent contractor of the Trust, (ii) Consultant shall not have any right to act for, represent or otherwise bind the Trust in any manner and (iii) except as otherwise provided herein, Consultant shall not be entitled to, and hereby waives all claims to, any of the rights, privileges or benefits of an employee of the Trust or any of the Trust’s affiliates. If Consultant were to be reclassified by a state or federal agency or court as the Trust’s employee under applicable law or otherwise with respect to the provision of Services hereunder, Consultant will not be eligible to receive any employee benefits from the Trust, except those mandated by state or federal law, even if by the terms of the Company’s benefit plans or programs in effect at the time of such reclassification, Consultant would otherwise be eligible for such benefits. (c) Consultant shall determine the method, details and means of performing the Services and shall devote the amount of time reasonably necessary in [his][her] judgment to perform the Services. The Trust and Consultant shall mutually agree upon the specific hours of availability for performance of Services to the extent such specificity is necessary for the performance of such Services. Services shall be performed at one or more location(s), including remotely, to be determined by Consultant. 4. Consulting Fee; Reimbursement . During the Term, for the Services provided under this Agreement, the Trust shall pay Consultant a fee of $[250][300] per hour, calculated in whole hour increments (the “ Consulting Fee ”). Consultant will bill the Trust periodically (usually monthly) for the Services. Payment will be due within 30 days of the date of the billing statement. Consultant may charge interest on amounts which are overdue for more than 30 days. Interest will be calculated at 12% per year or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is lower. Consultant shall also be reimbursed for all reasonable out-of-pocket expenses properly incurred in connection with the Services provided hereunder, which out-of-pocket expenses shall not exceed $2,500 without the prior written approval of the Trust. Such reimbursements shall be promptly provided to Consultant. 5. Release of Claims . Consultant, on his or her own behalf, and on behalf of his or her heirs, agents, family members, executors, administrators, representatives, attorneys, successors and assigns, hereby fully and forever releases and discharges the Trust, the Company, and any and all of their past, present, or future parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, and related entities, and any and all of their past, present or future officers, directors, members, employees, agents, counsel, consultants, auditors, contractors, successors and assigns, including, but not limited to, Washington Real Estate Investment Trust (the “ Trust Releasees ”), from any and all complaints, claims, demands, damages, lawsuits, and causes of action, whether known, unknown or unforeseen, arising out of or in connection with any event, transaction or matter occurring or existing on or before the date of Consultant’s execution of this Agreement, which Consultant has or may have against any of them for any reason whatsoever in law or in equity, under federal, state, local or other law, whether the same be upon statutory claim, contract, tort or other basis, including but not limited to any and all claims arising from or relating to Consultant’s past employment or termination of employment; any and all claims relating to wages, salary, bonuses, commissions, other compensation, expenses, benefits, leave, discrimination, disabilities, accommodation, harassment, or retaliation or other wrongful conduct; and any and all claims relating to any employment contract, express or implied. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, this release covers any and all claims under the Civil Rights Acts of 1866 and 1964, the Americans with Disabilities Act, the Equal Pay Act, the National Labor Relations Act, the Family and Medical Leave Act, the Fair Labor Standards Act, the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act, the Employee Retirement Income Security Act, the Maryland Fair Employment Practices Act, the Maryland Parental Leave Act, the Maryland Equal Pay for Equal Work Law, the Maryland Healthy Working Families Act, all as amended and including all of their respective implementing regulations, and any other federal, state or local statutes related to Consultant’s past employment. 2 This release covers claims Consultant knows about and those Consultant does not know about but does not waive or release any claims or rights that arise after Consultant executes this Agreement. Consultant agrees, without limiting the generality of the above release, not to file any claim or lawsuit seeking monetary recovery or other relief based on any claims that are lawfully released in this Section. Consultant further hereby irrevocably and unconditionally waives any and all rights to recover, and will not accept, any monetary or other relief concerning the claims that are lawfully released in this Section. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Consultant is not releasing (a) any right to enforce this Agreement; (b) any claim under the Age Discrimination in Employment Act; or (c) any claims for unemployment compensation, workers’ compensation benefits or other rights or claims that may not be released by this Section as a matter of law. Additionally, Consultant is not releasing any rights Consultant may have in the nature of indemnification or coverage under a directors and officers insurance policy, which shall apply in accordance with their terms. Consultant represents and understands that the foregoing is a GENERAL RELEASE. 6. Rights Not Subject to Limitation . Notwithstanding any other provisions of this Agreement, this Agreement does not limit any right Consultant, the Trust, or the Company may have that may not be limited by private agreement, including any right to: (a) provide any information in response to a valid subpoena, court order, other legal process or as otherwise required to be provided by law; (b) challenge the validity or enforceability of Section 5; (c) file a charge with, provide information to, or participate in an investigation or proceeding conducted by a government agency authorized to enforce laws against unlawful conduct, provided that Section 5 does waive, to the maximum extent permitted by law, any right to seek, recover or accept any monetary payments or other individual relief for Consultant connected to any agency or other action related to claims that are lawfully released in Section 5; or (d) report possible violations of federal or state law or regulation to any governmental agency or entity or self-regulatory organization or to cooperate with such agency, entity, or organization, without notice to the Trust (and to receive a whistleblower award provided by law for providing such information). The Parties acknowledge that pursuant to 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b), an individual may not be held liable under any criminal or civil federal or state trade secret law for disclosure of a trade secret: (i) made in confidence to a government official, either directly or indirectly, or to an attorney, solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law or (ii) in a complaint or other document filed in a lawsuit or other proceeding, if such filing is made under seal. An individual who files a lawsuit for retaliation by an employer for reporting a suspected violation of law may disclose the trade secret to the individual’s attorney and use the trade secret information in the court proceeding, provided that the individual files any document containing the trade secret under seal and does not disclose the trade secret except pursuant to court order. 7. Termination of Services . Consultant’s services may be terminated (a) by the mutual written agreement of the Parties; (b) by the Trust or by Consultant at any time for any reason or no reason upon at least thirty (30) days’ advance written notice to the other Party hereto; (c) by the Trust due to any material breach of this Agreement by Consultant and such breach is not cured within ten (10) days following the Trust’s delivery of written notice to Consultant of such breach; or (d) by Consultant due to any material breach of this Agreement by the Trust and such breach is not cured within ten (10) days following Consultant’s delivery of written notice to the Trust of such breach; provided , however , that Consultant’s services shall automatically terminate upon Consultant’s death. Upon termination of Consultant’s services hereunder, the Trust shall have no further obligation to provide compensation to Consultant hereunder except for (i) reimbursement for any reasonable out-of-pocket expenses properly incurred in connection with the Services through the date Consultant’s services are terminated, and (ii) the balance of any Consulting Fee owed through the date of termination that has not been previously paid. 3 8. Confidentiality . Consultant shall not disclose or use at any time, either during the Term or for a period of one (1) year thereafter, any Confidential Information of which Consultant is or becomes aware, whether or not such information is developed by Consultant, except to the extent that such disclosure or use is directly related to and required by Consultant’s performance in good faith of duties assigned to Consultant by the Trust. Consultant will take all appropriate steps within Consultant’s control to safeguard Confidential Information in Consultant’s possession and to protect it against disclosure, misuse, espionage, loss and theft. Consultant shall, at [his][her] option, either destroy (and shall certify such destruction in writing to the Trust) or deliver to the Trust promptly following the expiration of the Term, or at any time the Trust may request, all memoranda, notes, plans, records, reports and other documents and data (and copies thereof) relating to the Confidential Information of the business of the Trust that Consultant may then possess or have under Consultant’s control. As used herein, the term “ Confidential Information ” means information that is not generally known to the public and that is used, developed or obtained by the Trust in connection with its business, including, but not limited to, information, observations and data obtained by Consultant during the Term or while performing Services to the Trust pursuant to this Agreement concerning the business of the Trust, its products or services, its cost and pricing structures, financial information, accounting and business methods, inventions, customers and clients and customer or client lists, customer and supplier information and any similar and related information in whatever form. Confidential Information will not include any information that has been published in a form generally available to the public (except as a result of Consultant’s unauthorized disclosure) prior to the date Consultant discloses or uses such information. Confidential Information will not be deemed to have been published or otherwise disclosed merely because individual portions of the information have been separately published, but only if all material features comprising such information have been published in combination. 9. Indemnification . During the Term and thereafter, the Trust agrees to indemnify and hold Consultant and Consultant’s heirs and representatives harmless, to the maximum extent permitted by law, against any and all damages, costs, liabilities, losses and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees) as a result of any claim or proceeding (whether civil, criminal, administrative or investigative), or any threatened claim or proceeding (whether civil, criminal, administrative or investigative), against Consultant that arises out of or relates to the performance of Consultant’s Services hereunder at the request of the Trust, and to advance to Consultant or Consultant’s heirs or representatives such reasonable expenses upon written request with appropriate documentation of such expense upon receipt of an undertaking by Consultant or on Consultant’s behalf to repay such amount if it shall ultimately be determined under applicable law or pursuant to the immediately following sentence that Consultant is not entitled to be indemnified by the Trust. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Consultant shall not be entitled to indemnification hereunder to the extent any claim or proceeding (or threatened claim or proceeding) arises out of Consultant’s gross negligence, bad faith, fraud or willful misconduct. The Trust shall be entitled to assume the defense of any such proceeding and Consultant will use reasonable efforts to cooperate with such defense. To the extent that Consultant in good faith determines that there is an actual or potential conflict of interest between the Trust and Consultant in connection with the defense of a proceeding, Consultant shall so notify the Trust and shall be entitled to separate representation at the Trust’s expense by counsel selected by Consultant (provided that the Trust may reasonably object to the selection of counsel within ten (10) business days after notification thereof) which counsel shall cooperate, and coordinate the defense, with the Trust’s counsel and minimize the expense of such separate representation to the extent consistent with Consultant’s separate defense. This Section 9 shall continue in effect after the termination of Consultant’s consultancy or the termination of this Agreement. 10. Representations of Consultant . Consultant represents, warrants and covenants that as of the date hereof: (a) Consultant has the full right, authority and capacity to enter into this Agreement and perform Consultant’s obligations hereunder; (b) Consultant is not bound by any agreement that conflicts with or prevents or restricts the full performance by Consultant of the Services or Consultant’s obligations to the Trust hereunder during or after the Term; and (c) the execution and delivery of this Agreement shall not result in any breach or violation of, or a default under, any existing obligation, commitment or agreement to which Consultant is subject. 4 11. Taxes . Consultant shall be responsible for the payment of [his][her] portion of any and all required federal, state, local and foreign taxes (including self-employment taxes) incurred, or to be incurred, in connection with any amounts payable to Consultant under this Agreement. Consultant shall make such tax payments as may be required by applicable law and agrees to indemnify and hold the Trust harmless from any liability the Trust may incur resulting from or arising out of Consultant’s failure to make such tax payments. 12. Assignment . This Agreement shall not be assignable by Consultant without the prior written consent of the Trust, and any assignment in violation of this Agreement shall be void; provided , however , that the Trust shall not unreasonably withhold consent to Consultant’s assignment of this Agreement to a business entity or personal services company owned and managed by Consultant for purposes of Consultant personally providing the services hereunder through such entity or company. The Trust may assign this Agreement, and its rights and obligations hereunder, to any of its affiliates. This Agreement shall be binding on, and shall inure to the benefit of, the parties to it and their respective heirs, legal representatives, successors and permitted assigns. Consultant acknowledges and agrees that all of Consultant’s covenants and obligations to the Trust, as well as the rights of the Trust hereunder, shall run in favor of and shall be enforceable by the Trust and its successors and assigns. 13. Governing Law . THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE GOVERNED BY AND CONSTRUED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE LAWS OF THE STATE OF MARYLAND APPLICABLE TO AGREEMENTS MADE AND TO BE WHOLLY PERFORMED WITHIN THAT STATE, WITHOUT REGARD TO ITS CONFLICT OF LAWS PROVISIONS OR THE CONFLICT OF LAWS PROVISIONS OF ANY OTHER JURISDICTION WHICH WOULD CAUSE THE APPLICATION OF ANY LAW OTHER THAN THAT OF THE STATE OF MARYLAND. Each Party to this Agreement irrevocably agrees for the exclusive benefit of the other that any and all suits, actions or proceedings relating to this Agreement (collectively, “ Proceedings ” and, individually, a “ Proceeding ”) may be maintained in either the courts of the State of Maryland or the federal District Courts located in the State of Maryland (collectively, the “ Chosen Courts ”) and that the Chosen Courts shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine or settle any such Proceeding and that any such Proceedings may be brought in the Chosen Courts. Each Party irrevocably waives any objection that it may have now or hereafter to the laying of the venue of any Proceedings in the Chosen Courts and any claim that any Proceedings have been brought in an inconvenient forum and further irrevocably agrees that a judgment in any Proceeding brought in the Chosen Courts shall be conclusive and binding upon it and may be enforced in the courts of any other jurisdiction. 14. Modification . This Agreement may not be modified or amended, nor may any rights under it be waived, except in a writing signed and agreed to by the Parties. 15. Severability . In the event that any provision of this Agreement is determined to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining terms and conditions of this Agreement shall be unaffected and shall remain in full force and effect. In addition, if any provision is determined to be invalid or unenforceable due to its duration and/or scope, the duration and/or scope of such provision, as the case may be, shall be reduced, such reduction shall be to the smallest extent necessary to comply with applicable law, and such provision shall be enforceable, in its reduced form, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law. 16. Survival . The rights and obligations of the Parties under the provisions of this Agreement shall survive, and remain binding and enforceable, notwithstanding the expiration of the Term, the termination of this Agreement, the termination of Consultant’s services hereunder or any settlement of the financial rights and obligations arising from Consultant’s services hereunder, to the extent necessary to preserve the intended benefits of such provisions. 5 17. Notices . Any notice given pursuant to this Agreement to any Party hereto shall be deemed to have been duly given when mailed by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, or by overnight courier, or by e-mail, facsimile or telecopy, or when hand delivered as follows: If to the Trust: Mark Chertok Elme Communities Liquidating Trust c/o FTI Consulting, Inc. 56 Livingston Avenue, Suite 400 Roseland, NJ 07068 *** and ELMETrustee@fticonsulting.com If to Consultant: [Address] E-mail: [___] or at such other address as either Party shall from time to time designate by written notice, in the manner provided herein, to the other Party hereto. 18. Counterparts . This Agreement may be executed by one or more of the Parties hereto on any number of separate counterparts and all such counterparts shall be deemed to be one and the same instrument. Each Party hereto confirms that any facsimile copy of such Party’s executed counterpart of the Agreement (or its signature page thereof) shall be deemed to be an executed original thereof. [ Signature Page Follows ] 6 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, this Agreement has been duly executed by the Parties as of the date first written above. ELME COMMUNITIES LIQUIDATING TRUST By: Name: Mark E. Chertok Title: Trustee CONSULTANT By: [Name]

text: EX-10.1 2 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT – HYORC / MCKINNEY This Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (the “Agreement”) is entered into effective as of the last date of signature below (the “Effective Date”) by (i) HyOrc Corporation, a Wyoming corporation formerly known as Asia Properties, Inc. (“HyOrc”); (ii) Daniel S. McKinney, also identified in the Action as Daniel McKinney (“McKinney”), individually; and (iii) Coldway Limited, LLC (“Coldway”), acting through its duly authorized representative. HyOrc, McKinney, and Coldway are the “Parties.” The five individual defendants identified below are protected Released Persons and intended third-party beneficiaries, but are not executing parties and are not deemed to make any representation, grant any release, or assume any personal obligation by reason of this Agreement. RECITALS A. McKinney filed an action styled Daniel McKinney v. HyOrc Corporation, et al., Case No. A-26-955028-C, in the Eighth Judicial District Court, Clark County, Nevada, Department 30 (the “Action”). The operative First Amended Complaint names HyOrc and K. Reginal Fubara, Andrea Magalini, Manoharan Sundaralingam, James Anthony McNaught-Davis, and Richard Oblatah, identified by HyOrc as Richard Oblath (together, the “Individual Defendants”). B. The Action concerns, among other things, the affiliate/control classification of McKinney and Coldway on the records of Transfer Online, Inc. (“Transfer Online”), and proposed deposits, transfers, or sales of HyOrc securities. This subject matter, including claims concerning the May–June 2026 communications and any asserted resulting injury through the Effective Date, is the “Dispute.” C. McKinney and Coldway contend that they are not HyOrc affiliates. HyOrc disputes liability and denies that it imposed a separate blanket prohibition on lawful transfers. Without resolving the disputed historical facts, the Parties desire to settle the Dispute, dismiss the Action with prejudice as to every defendant, and provide Transfer Online with only the narrowly limited affiliate/control classification instruction attached as Exhibit A. D. No Party will pay money to another as settlement consideration. The consideration consists of the reciprocal covenants, releases, factual representations, limited instruction, and dismissal set forth below. The Parties acknowledge the sufficiency of that consideration. 1. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF MCKINNEY AND COLDWAY 1.1 Separate and joint undertakings. McKinney makes the representations below individually; Coldway makes them through its authorized representative. Each represents and warrants to HyOrc and to the Individual Defendants, as intended beneficiaries, that each statement concerning that person or entity is true on the Effective Date and will remain true when the Exhibit A instruction is delivered. McKinney and Coldway acknowledge that HyOrc will rely materially upon these representations in issuing that instruction. Page 1 1.2 Nonaffiliate status and control. McKinney asserts he is not an affiliate of HyOrc under the definition in 17 C.F.R. § 230.144(a)(1), nor has he been an affiliate during the 90-day period preceding the Effective Date or, if later, the delivery date of Exhibit A. Neither, alone or together with any person acting in concert, directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with HyOrc. Neither has any presently exercisable legal or practical power to direct or cause the direction of HyOrc’s management or policies through securities ownership, agreement, proxy, appointment right, financing arrangement, informal understanding, coordinated action, or otherwise. 1.3 No undisclosed arrangements. Neither McKinney nor Coldway is a party to, or beneficiary of, any undisclosed oral or written voting agreement, proxy, shareholder agreement, board appointment or removal arrangement, management or consulting arrangement, veto right, side letter, financing or economic arrangement, agreement to act in concert, or other relationship that confers direct or indirect control of HyOrc or materially bears on affiliate status. Each has disclosed in writing to HyOrc any exception material to that determination before signing. Mere historical contact with management is not represented to be nonexistent; the representation concerns present status and the specified 90-day lookback. 1.4 Accuracy of opinion information. McKinney and Coldway have reviewed the May 20, 2026 letter from John L. Stoss, P.C., addressed to Wilson-Davis & Company and Transfer Online (the “Opinion Letter”). To the best of their actual knowledge after reasonable inquiry, all factual information furnished by or for them on which the Opinion Letter’s affiliate-status analysis relies was materially accurate when given, and neither knowingly omitted information material to the nonaffiliate analysis. They have disclosed to HyOrc in writing before execution any material factual change or inaccuracy of which they are aware. They do not represent that the Opinion Letter is an unconditional authorization to resell any securities. 1.5 No concealed relationship or plans. Neither McKinney nor Coldway is knowingly using another person or entity to exercise control over HyOrc, and neither has any undisclosed existing agreement or plan that would render the representations in Sections 1.2–1.4 materially misleading. They will promptly notify HyOrc and Transfer Online in writing if, before the classification change is implemented, any material representation becomes inaccurate. 1.6 Power, ownership and enforceability. McKinney has legal capacity to sign for himself; the person signing for Coldway has authority under its governing documents to bind Coldway. McKinney and Coldway have authority to release the claims they purport to release, including claims they assert individually, beneficially, through Coldway, or through another person acting by or through them. They have not assigned any claim within the Dispute; if any assignment exists, they shall identify it before closing and obtain a binding release from the assignee as a condition to HyOrc’s delivery of Exhibit A. 1.7 No issuer clearance of specific securities. McKinney and Coldway acknowledge that neither this Agreement nor Exhibit A determines whether particular shares are restricted, whether a restrictive legend is removable, whether a particular sale or deposit satisfies federal law, whether an exemption from registration is available, or whether a transfer agent or broker must process a particular transaction. They remain responsible for obtaining any required transfer-specific legal opinions and complying with applicable law. Page 2 2. HYORC UNDERTAKING 2.1 Transfer Agent Letter letter. Subject to Section 4, HyOrc will sign and send to Transfer Online the letter in the exact form attached as Exhibit A, without material modification absent written agreement of the Parties. The letter states HyOrc’s present belief, based on the Opinion Letter to the extent applicable and McKinney’s and Coldway’s warranties and representations, that they are not HyOrc affiliates and authorizes removal solely of their affiliate/control designations from Transfer Online’s records. 2.2 No broader instruction. HyOrc does not agree to adopt or issue a securities-law opinion; and does not warrant that particular shares may be deposited, transferred, or sold. No such undertaking may be implied from the letter. Transfer Online retains its own lawful compliance duties and procedures. HyOrc does not guarantee Transfer Online’s implementation, any broker acceptance, or any sale result. 2.3 No continuing certification. Any new request involving transfer-specific compliance, new or changed facts, or a future control relationship must be evaluated independently. HyOrc has no ongoing obligation to certify nonaffiliate status after it has sent Exhibit A, except to correct any communication it learns was materially inaccurate when issued. 3. DISMISSAL AND SETTLEMENT DOCUMENTS 3.1 Complete dismissal. McKinney shall cause the Action, including all claims against HyOrc and each of the five Individual Defendants, to be dismissed WITH PREJUDICE, on the merits and without an award of attorneys’ fees or costs to any litigant. The dismissal must resolve the entire Action, not only selected claims or defendants. McKinney shall not commence or support a substantially duplicative suit concerning the Dispute in any forum, and Coldway shall not commence or support such a suit. 3.2 Stipulation. The Parties will arrange execution of a Stipulation for Dismissal With Prejudice, substantially in the separately prepared companion form, pursuant to NRCP 41(a)(1)(A)(ii), signed by all parties who have appeared in the Action through counsel or directly, as required. HyOrc’s signature to this Agreement alone does not signify that it acts as legal counsel or authorized representative for any Individual Defendant. Any separate appearance or signature required from an Individual Defendant for the court filing must be obtained through appropriate counsel or directly. 3.3 Dismissal processing. Counsel responsible for filing shall complete any necessary local-rule statements regarding scheduling/trial dates and shall deliver the stipulation to Department 30 chambers before filing as required by EDCR 2.91. Following delivery to chambers, counsel shall file the stipulation promptly and circulate conformed copies. If the court requests a dismissal order rather than accepting the stipulation alone, the Parties shall promptly submit a conforming order without modifying the substantive settlement. Page 3 4. COORDINATED CLOSING AND DELIVERY OF EXHIBIT A 4.1 Closing prerequisites. Closing occurs only after all signatories have signed, including McKinney has executed this Agreement individually and Coldway through an authorized representative, and HyOr has signed. These items may be delivered electronically to counsel. No director is required to execute this private Agreement. 4.2 Exchange. As soon as practicable after all prerequisites are satisfied, the Parties’ counsel shall coordinate one closing exchange: (i) McKinney’s counsel delivers the stipulation to Department 30 chambers, files it as required by EDCR 2.91, and transmits filing confirmation; and (ii) HyOrc, acting through Fubara or authorized counsel, sends the signed Exhibit A letter directly to Transfer Online, copying McKinney’s counsel. The Parties may release the dismissal for filing and the Exhibit A letter contemporaneously on mutually confirmed instructions. Neither counsel may intentionally release its deliverable in advance of an assurance that the reciprocal deliverable is ready for immediate release. 4.3 Effect of signatures and closing. The releases, covenants not to sue, warranties, and indemnities in this Agreement become binding and enforceable immediately upon execution by all three Parties, notwithstanding administrative delay in filing the stipulation or transmitting Exhibit A. A failure to carry out a required closing act is enforceable by specific performance and other available remedies and does not restore a released claim. No settlement letter shall be issued merely upon an unsigned draft, or before McKinney and Coldway have signed and the complete dismissal document is in counsel’s possession. 4.4 Transfer-agent response. If Transfer Online requires additional documentation or declines to modify its coding, HyOrc shall reasonably confirm the authenticity and scope of Exhibit A but is not required to expand that instruction, issue an issuer counsel opinion, alter another restriction, litigate with Transfer Online, or guarantee a result. Any additional action requires a separate writing signed by HyOrc. 5. RELEASES; COVENANTS NOT TO SUE; BENEFICIARIES 5.1 McKinney/Coldway release. McKinney and Coldway, each for itself/himself and, to the fullest extent legally effective, for its/his predecessors, successors, heirs, administrators, representatives, affiliates, owners, managers, officers, members, assigns, and persons claiming by or through it/him (collectively the “McKinney Releasing Persons”), irrevocably release and forever discharge HyOrc, Asia Properties, Inc., Fubara, Magalini, Sundaralingam, McNaught-Davis, and Richard Oblath (including the person sued as “Richard Oblatah”), and each of their respective past and present parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, predecessors, successors, directors, officers, employees, managers, agents, counsel, insurers, representatives, and assigns (the “HyOrc Released Persons”) from every claim, liability, debt, demand, action, damage, expense, attorney fee, or cause of action, known or unknown, fixed or contingent, arising from or relating to the Dispute or facts occurring on or before the Effective Date that were asserted or could have been asserted in connection with the affiliate/control designation, the May–June 2026 transfer request, the alleged impediment to deposit/sale, and any resulting alleged loss. This is a release of existing claims, not a prospective waiver of compliance with future securities laws. Page 4 5.2 HyOrc release. HyOrc, solely for itself and not purporting to bind any Individual Defendant in an individual capacity, irrevocably releases McKinney and Coldway and their respective heirs, representatives, officers, managers, successors and assigns (the “McKinney Released Persons”) from claims that HyOrc owns arising from the same Dispute and based on facts occurring on or before the Effective Date. HyOrc does not waive a claim arising under this Agreement or from materially inaccurate representations made as part of it. 5.3 Covenants not to sue. McKinney and Coldway covenant not to file, maintain, finance, direct, voluntarily assist, or cause another person to prosecute any released claim against any HyOrc Released Person. HyOrc covenants not to prosecute a claim it releases under Section 5.2. This does not prevent compliance with a subpoena, compulsory legal process, or nonwaivable regulatory duties; the responding party shall, when lawful, provide reasonable advance notice. 5.4 Exceptions. Nothing releases (a) rights and obligations created by this Agreement, including indemnification and enforcement; (b) ownership of securities or otherwise lawful future rights as a shareholder, subject to applicable law; (c) claims based exclusively on acts occurring after the Effective Date; (d) obligations under an unrelated written agreement not specifically addressing the Dispute; or (e) any right or obligation that law prohibits the Parties from waiving. No person releases claims it does not legally possess. 5.5 Named directors; third-party beneficiaries. The five Individual Defendants named in Section 5.1, including Richard Oblath, are express and intended third-party beneficiaries of Sections 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 10 and may enforce the releases, covenants, and indemnity in their own names. They are not signatories, do not grant releases of their individual claims, and do not consent to general personal jurisdiction or assume duties solely because they receive these protections. HyOrc represents that Fubara signs for HyOrc alone and not as agent for the other Defendants. 6. JOINT AND SEVERAL INDEMNIFICATION 6.1 Scope. McKinney and Coldway, jointly and severally, shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless HyOrc and the HyOrc Released Persons (each an “Indemnified Person”) from and against all actual losses, liabilities, judgments, settlements, penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, reasonable attorneys’ fees and defense costs, and reasonable investigation and enforcement expenses (collectively “Losses”), including third-party claims, but only to the extent arising from (i) a materially false, misleading, or incomplete representation or warranty made by McKinney or Coldway in this Agreement; (ii) an undisclosed agreement, understanding, or arrangement conferring direct or indirect control that renders a Section 1 representation materially inaccurate; or (iii) a breach by McKinney or Coldway of a covenant in this Agreement. Losses include reasonable costs of defending third-party proceedings arising from those matters. 6.2 Exclusion. No indemnity is owed for any portion of Losses attributable to the Indemnified Person’s own fraud or willful misconduct. Nothing requires or permits indemnification of an amount that applicable law prohibits. The indemnity does not apply merely because the transfer agent declines to act or because a dispute about legal interpretation arises, absent a triggering representation breach or covenant breach under Section 6.1. Page 5 6.3 Claims process. An Indemnified Person shall give reasonably prompt written notice of a claim; delayed notice relieves the indemnitors only to the extent materially prejudiced. The indemnitors may assume a third-party defense with qualified counsel reasonably acceptable to the Indemnified Person, provided there is no material conflict of interest and they acknowledge the defense obligation in writing. An Indemnified Person may retain separate counsel at its own expense, except that reasonable separate-counsel fees are covered when counsel reasonably determines a material conflict exists or the defense is not diligently conducted. No settlement imposing an admission, nonmonetary obligation, or unreleased liability on an Indemnified Person may be entered without that person’s written consent, not unreasonably withheld for a settlement consisting solely of money paid by indemnitors and a complete release. The Indemnified Person shall reasonably mitigate Losses. Indemnity obligations survive dismissal and fulfillment of Section 4, subject to applicable limitation periods. 7. COSTS, NONADMISSION, AND RIGHTS PRESERVED 7.1 No cash payment; fees. No Party shall pay monetary settlement consideration. Each Party shall bear its own attorneys’ fees, expenses, and taxable costs incurred in the Action and negotiation/performance of this Agreement, except amounts recoverable under Section 6 for later breaches or indemnified claims. The stipulation expressly supersedes any default repayment of filing fees otherwise implicated by NRCP 41(a)(1)(C). 7.2 No admission. Settlement, delivery of Exhibit A, dismissal, and the terms of this Agreement are compromises of contested claims and do not constitute an admission of wrongdoing, negligence, breach of duty, unlawful transfer restriction, or liability by HyOrc or any Individual Defendant, or any admission by McKinney or Coldway regarding past affiliate status. 7.3 Regulatory rights. Nothing requires any person to make a false securities disclosure, suppress a required report, waive nonwaivable securities-law rights, or interfere with duties of Transfer Online, a broker, or a regulator. No general legend-removal or marketability warranty is given. 8. AUTHORITY, ENFORCEMENT AND GOVERNING LAW 8.1 Signatures and capacity. Fubara represents that he is authorized to enter this Agreement for HyOrc and issue Exhibit A on its behalf. McKinney represents that he signs individually and has authority, in the designated capacity shown below, to bind Coldway. Each Party has had the opportunity to consult independent counsel and has read and understood this Agreement. 8.2 Governing law. Nevada law governs interpretation and enforcement of this settlement contract, without altering the federal securities laws, Wyoming law governing HyOrc, or the issuer-jurisdiction rules governing securities-transfer duties. This choice-of-law provision does not constitute an admission that Nevada courts had personal jurisdiction over HyOrc or the Individual Defendants for the underlying Action. Page 6 8.3 Limited enforcement forum. Solely for an action between signatories to enforce or interpret this Agreement, the signatory Parties consent to personal jurisdiction and venue in a court of competent jurisdiction in Clark County, Nevada. The Individual Defendants are not deemed to consent to jurisdiction by virtue of being third-party beneficiaries. The Parties may seek specific performance, damages, and other available relief for breach. The dismissal does not itself reserve jurisdiction in the Action unless the court independently orders otherwise. 8.4 Entire agreement; modification. This Agreement, including Exhibit A, is the entire agreement concerning the Dispute and supersedes contemporaneous settlement negotiations about it. It does not rescind any unrelated earlier agreement or release. Amendments and waivers must be written and signed by all Parties. No delay is a waiver. If any provision is unenforceable, the remainder survives to the extent consistent with the essential exchange; the Parties shall replace the provision with a lawful equivalent. 8.5 Successors; no transfer of claims. This Agreement binds and benefits signatories and their lawful successors and assigns. No Party may assign an obligation under it without the other Parties’ prior written consent, except that protected persons retain their express third-party-beneficiary rights. No assignment may revive a released claim. 8.6 Counterparts and electronic signatures. Signatures exchanged by PDF or a recognized electronic-signature service are effective as originals; this Agreement may be signed in counterparts. Titles and headings are for convenience. “Including” means “including without limitation.” All Parties participated in negotiating the text; no presumption against the drafter applies. 8.7 Notices. Settlement notices must be in writing and may be transmitted by email to counsel who most recently appeared or communicated for the receiving Party in the Action, with a direct copy to that Party at its last designated notice address. A notice is effective when its receipt is affirmatively acknowledged or when delivered by a nationally recognized overnight courier. A Party may designate a replacement address by written notice. Page 7 SIGNATURES IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties execute this Agreement as of the dates set out below. The last signature date is the Effective Date. HYORC CORPORATION DANIEL S. MCKINNEY, INDIVIDUALLY /s/ K. Reginald Fubara Name: K. Reginald Fubara, /s/ Daniel S. McKinney Chief Executive Officer, solely for HyOrc Corporation Date: 10/30/2026 Date: 11/02/2026 COLDWAY LIMITED, LLC /s/ Daniel S. McKinney Name: Daniel S. McKinney, Manager / authorized representative Date: 10/30/2026 Page 8 EXHIBIT A FORM OF LIMITED TRANSFER-AGENT INSTRUCTION Via email to Transfer Online, Inc. Attn: Bryan Cochran / Veronica Castro-Luna 512 SE Salmon Street, 2nd Floor Portland, Oregon 97214-3444 Re: HyOrc Corporation Affiliate/Control Designation for Daniel S. McKinney and Coldway Limited, LLC Transfer Online: HyOrc Corporation has considered the May 20, 2026 opinion letter of John L. Stoss, P.C. concerning Coldway Limited, LLC and the written representations and warranties provided to HyOrc by Daniel S. McKinney and Coldway Limited, LLC denying affiliate status. In reliance on that opinion to the extent applicable and those representations and warranties, HyOrc does not presently believe that Daniel S. McKinney is an “affiliate” of HyOrc within the meaning of Rule 144 under the Securities Act of 1933. Accordingly, HyOrc authorizes and requests that Transfer Online remove the existing affiliate designation from its records for Daniel S. McKinney and for Coldway Limited, LLC. This authorization is not an opinion on the eligibility of any specific securities or transaction for resale or transfer. Sincerely, HYORC CORPORATION For delivery only upon satisfaction of the closing procedure in Section 4 of the Agreement. Page 9

text: EX-10.1 2 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 AMENDMENT NO. 3 TO SENIOR SECURED LOAN AND SECURITY AGREEMENT THIS AMENDMENT NO. 3 TO SENIOR SECURED LOAN AND SECURITY AGREEMENT dated as of November 6, 2026 (this “ Amendment ”) is made by and among Reed’s, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the “ Borrower ”), the Guarantors party hereto, the Lenders party hereto and Cantor Fitzgerald Securities, as administrative agent and collateral agent for the Lenders (in such capacities, the “ Administrative Agent ”). RECITALS A. The Borrower, the Lenders and the Administrative Agent are parties to the Senior Secured Loan and Security Agreement dated as of November 14, 2024 (as amended by that certain Amendment No. 1 to Senior Secured Loan and Security Agreement dated as of September 26, 2025, as amended by that certain Amendment No. 2 to Senior Secured Loan and Security Agreement, dated as of September 30, 2026, and as further amended, restated, amended and restated, supplemented or modified from time to time prior to the date hereof, the “ Existing Credit Agreement ”, and as amended by this Amendment, the “ Credit Agreement ”). Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings given them in the Credit Agreement. B. Pursuant to Section 12.5(a) of the Existing Credit Agreement, the Borrower has requested that the Lenders make certain amendments to the Existing Credit Agreement, in each case as set forth herein. C. The Administrative Agent and the Lenders party hereto, constituting all of the Required Lenders immediately prior to giving effect to the effectiveness of this Amendment (the “ Consenting Lenders ”), have agreed to amend the Existing Credit Agreement on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth herein. Accordingly, in consideration of the mutual agreements herein contained and other good and valuable consideration, the sufficiency and receipt of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto agree as follows: Section 1. Existing Credit Agreement Amendment (a) The Borrower, the other Credit Parties, the Lenders and the Administrative Agent hereby agree that, effective as of the Amendment No. 3 Effective Date (defined below), the Existing Credit Agreement shall be amended as follows: (i) Section 1 of the Existing Credit Agreement is hereby amended to add the following definitions in appropriate alphabetical order: “ Amendment No. 3 ” means that certain Amendment No. 3 to Senior Secured Loan and Security Agreement, dated as of the Amendment No. 3 Effective Date, by and among the Borrower, the Guarantors party thereto, the Lenders party thereto, the Administrative Agent and the Collateral Agent. “ Amendment No. 3 Effective Date ” means November 6, 2026. “ Cash / Inventory / AR Liquidity ” means the fair market value of each of the Qualified Cash, Inventory and accounts receivable owned by the Credit Parties. (ii) Section 7.15 of the Existing Credit Agreement shall be deleted in its entirety and replaced with the following: “ 7.15. Cash / Inventory / AR Liquidity . Permit (i) during the period from and including the Amendment No. 3 Effective Date to the date on which the Borrower receives cash equity contributions in an aggregate amount of at least Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($2,500,000) following the Amendment No. 3 Effective Date (the “ Increased Liquidity Period ”), the Cash / Inventory / AR Liquidity at any time to be less than Eleven Million Dollars ($11,000,000) and (ii) following the Increased Liquidity Period, the Cash / Inventory / AR Liquidity as of 11:59 p.m. (New York City Time) on the last day of each month to be less than Eleven Million Dollars ($11,000,000).” (iii) Section 8.13 of the Existing Credit Agreement shall be deleted in its entirety and replaced with the following: “ 8.13. Required Equity Contribution . The Borrower fails to receive cash equity contributions in an aggregate amount of at least Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($2,500,000) following the Amendment No. 3 Effective Date but on or prior to November 20, 2026.” Section 2. Representations and Warranties . To induce the other parties hereto to enter into this Amendment, each Credit Party represents and warrants to each of the Lenders and the Administrative Agent that immediately before and immediately after giving effect to this Amendment: (a) the execution, delivery and performance of this Amendment is within such Credit Party’s corporate or other organizational power and has been duly authorized by all necessary corporate or other organizational action of such Credit Party; this Amendment has been duly executed and delivered by such Credit Party and is a legal, valid and binding obligation of such Credit Party, enforceable in accordance with its terms; (b) the execution and delivery of this Amendment and the performance by such Credit Party hereof (a) does not require any consent or approval of, registration or filing with, or any other action by, any Governmental Authority, except (i) such as have been obtained or made and are in full force and effect and (ii) such consents, approvals, registrations, filings, or other actions the failure to obtain or make which could not be reasonably expected to have a Material Adverse Change, (b) will not violate any (i) of such Credit Party’s Operating Documents or (ii) Requirements of Law applicable to such Credit Party which violation, in the case of this clause (b)(ii), could reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Change and (c) will not violate or result in a default under any material contractual obligation to which such Credit Party is a party which violation, in the case of this clause (c), could reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Change; (c) no Default or Event of Default has occurred and is continuing; and (d) the representations and warranties set forth in Article 5 of the Existing Credit Agreement, as amended, are true and correct in all material respects on and as of the date hereof (and in all respects if any such representation or warranty is already qualified by materiality or Material Adverse Change), except to the extent such representations and warranties expressly relate to an earlier date, in which case such representations and warranties shall be true and correct in all material respects as of such earlier date. Section 3. Amendment Effectiveness . The effectiveness of this Amendment is subject to the satisfaction (or waiver in writing by the Consenting Lenders) of the following conditions (the date on which such conditions are satisfied or waived, the “ Amendment No. 3 Effective Date ”): (a) the receipt by the Administrative Agent of this Amendment executed and delivered by a duly authorized signatory of (i) the Borrower, (ii) each other Credit Party, (iii) the Administrative Agent and (iv) each Lender (which may include a copy transmitted by facsimile or other electronic method); and (b) as of the Amendment No. 3 Effective Date (immediately after giving effect to the effectiveness of this Amendment), the representations and warranties set forth in Section 2 hereof are true and correct in all material respects. Each Lender, by delivering its signature page to this Amendment, shall be deemed to have consented to, approved or accepted or to be satisfied with, each document required hereunder to be consented to, approved by or acceptable or satisfactory to a Lender. Section 4. Extension Fee The Borrower shall pay to Whitebox (or its designee) an extension fee in the amount of Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars ($25,000) (the “ Extension Fee ”), which Extension Fee shall be due and payable on or prior to November 20, 2026. The Extension Fee shall be fully earned on the Amendment No. 3 Effective Date, shall not be refundable for any reason whatsoever and shall not be subject to counterclaim or set-off. The failure of the Borrower to pay the Extension Fee when due shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 8.1 of the Credit Agreement. The Consenting Lenders consent to the payment of the Extension Fee. Section 5. Effect of Amendment . Nothing herein shall be deemed to entitle any Credit Party to a consent to, or a waiver, amendment, modification or other change of, any of the terms, conditions, obligations, covenants or agreements contained in the Existing Credit Agreement or any other Loan Document in similar or different circumstances. This Amendment shall constitute a “Loan Document” for all purposes of the Existing Credit Agreement, as amended hereby, and the other Loan Documents. Section 6. Counterparts . This Amendment may be executed by one or more of the parties to this Amendment on any number of separate counterparts, and all of said counterparts taken together shall be deemed to constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed signature page of this Amendment by facsimile or electronic (i.e., “pdf” or “tiff”) transmission shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart hereof. A set of the copies of this Amendment signed by all the parties shall be lodged with the Borrower and the Administrative Agent. Section 7. Governing Law , Etc . The terms of Sections 11.1 (Waiver of Jury Trial), 11.2 (Governing Law and Jurisdiction) and 11.3 (Submission to Jurisdiction) of the Existing Credit Agreement are hereby incorporated herein by reference, mutatis mutandis , and the parties hereto agree to such terms. Section 8. Headings . The headings of this Amendment are for purposes of reference only and shall not limit or otherwise affect the meaning hereof. Section 9. Direction to Administrative Agent . The undersigned Lenders party hereto (which constitute all of the Lenders) hereby (a) consent to the execution, delivery and performance by the Administrative Agent of this Amendment, (b) authorize and direct the Administrative Agent to execute and deliver this Amendment and such other documents as may be reasonably requested by the Borrower in connection therewith, and to perform its obligations thereunder, and (c) acknowledge and agree that the direction in this Section 9 constitutes a direction from the Required Lenders under the provisions of Article 9 of the Credit Agreement. The Credit Parties and the Lenders party hereto expressly agree and confirm that (a) the Administrative Agent’s right to indemnification, as set forth in Exhibit B of the Existing Credit Agreement, as amended, shall apply, in accordance with the terms thereof, with respect to any and all losses, claims, liabilities, costs and expenses that the Administrative Agent suffers, incurs or is threatened with relating to actions taken or omitted by the Administrative Agent in connection with this Amendment and the other Loan Documents, (b) all other rights, protections, privileges, immunities, exculpations, and indemnities afforded to the Administrative Agent under the Loan Documents shall apply to any and all actions taken or omitted by the Administrative Agent in connection with this Amendment and the other Loan Documents and (c) the Administrative Agent may conclusively rely upon (and shall be fully protected in relying upon) the Register in confirming that the Lenders party hereto constitute the Consenting Lenders on and as of the date hereof. Each undersigned Lender hereby severally represents and warrants to the Administrative Agent that, on and as of the date hereof, it is duly authorized to enter into this Amendment and perform its obligations hereunder. [Remainder of page left intentionally blank; signature pages follow.] IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties hereto have executed this Amendment as of the day and year first written above. REED’S, INC. , as the Borrower By: /s/ Douglas McCurdy Name: Douglas McCurdy Title: Chief Financial Officer [Signature Page to Amendment No. 3] CANTOR FITZGERALD SECURITIES , as Administrative Agent and Collateral Agent By: /s/ Christian Wall Name: Christian Wall Title: Global Head of Fixed Income Legal Reviewed Akin Newbraugh /s/ AN [Signature Page to Amendment No. 3] WHITEBOX RELATIVE VALUE PARTNERS, LP, as a Term Loan Lender and a Lender By: /s/ Andrew Thau Name: Andrew Thau Title: Managing Director WHITEBOX GT FUND, LP, as a Term Loan Lender and a Lender By: /s/ Andrew Thau Name: Andrew Thau Title: Managing Director WHITEBOX MULTI-STRATEGY PARTNERS, LP, as a Term Loan Lender and a Lender By: /s/ Andrew Thau Name: Andrew Thau Title: Managing Director PANDORA SELECT PARTNERS, LP, as a Term Loan Lender and a Lender By: /s/ Andrew Thau Name: Andrew Thau Title: Managing Director [Signature Page to Amendment No. 3]
