text: EX-10.1 3 capforceinc_ex10-1.htm EXHIBIT 10.1 Exhibit 10.1 Date: 27 October 2026 PRIVATE & CONFIDENTIAL CHRISTIAN-LAURENT BENOIT BONTE Dear Christian, RE: APPOINTMENT AS PRESIDENT, BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT The Executive Board is pleased to hereby notify you that the Executive Board has approved your recent application to transition from your current Chief Executive Officer role under the ‘officer’ classification to a more Business Development-aligned non-officer role as President, Business Development (“ BD President ”) for CapForce Inc. (“ CFOR ”) cum director of CapForce International (SG) Pte. Ltd. (“ CFI SG ”), effective 27 October 2026. CFOR and CFI SG shall be collectively referred to as “ Company ”. The position is offered on the following terms: 1. Terms of Employment 1.1. Your executive role will be redesignated from Chief Executive Officer to BD President with effect from 27 October 2026 (“ Effective Date ”), with the scope of responsibilities set out in this Letter. Your employment contract previously executed with CapForce International Holdings Ltd. (“ CFI Labuan ”) shall be transferred to CapForce International (SG) Pte. Ltd. (“ CFI SG ”) with effect from the Effective Date. Your appointment as Chief Executive Officer shall cease concurrently with your appointment as BD President of CapForce Inc. 1.2. Your continuous service shall be recognised from your original employment commencement date of 1 July 2025 with CFI Labuan. The six-month probationary period specified in your original Letter of Offer has completed, and no new probationary period shall apply as a result of the employment transfer and appointment under this Letter. 1.3. Your ordinary hours of work will be from Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 18:00. You are required to work at the designated workplace for three (3) days per week, with the remaining two (2) days under a remote working arrangement. You may be requested to work outside your normal working hours, including weekends and public holidays, where reasonably necessary to fulfil your duties and responsibilities. 2. Role/Duties 2.1. As BD President, you will be responsible for business development and advisory leadership across the across the Company’s global platform, with a focus on supporting the Head of Investment Banking Division (IBD) and Head of Asset & Wealth Management (AWM). You shall continue to have access to your TEAMS working account and email address. However, email records and all prior documents and information made available to you during your tenure as CEO shall only be retained solely to respond to any future SEC request or any shareholder or third-party litigation relation to the period wherein you served as CEO for CapForce Inc. 2.2. Your primary duties include, but are not limited to, the following: 2.2.1. Business Development ● Support and contribute to business development initiatives relevant to the IBD and AWM businesses. ● Identify and develop business opportunities aligned with the Company’s strategic objectives. ● Support the relevant business heads in developing and advancing business relationships and opportunities. 2.2.2. Corporate Development ● Support corporate development initiatives, including strategic opportunities and partnerships. ● Provide senior-level commercial and strategic input on relevant corporate development matters. 2.2.3. Transaction Advisory ● Provide senior-level advisory and commercial input on relevant transaction opportunities. ● Support transaction-related business development and advisory activities in coordination with the relevant business heads. 2.2.4. Executive Collaboration ● Maintain a peer-level working relationship with the Chief Executive Officer on business development, corporate development and transaction advisory matters. ● Provide leadership-level feedback and recommendations to the Chief Executive Officer on proposed initiatives, improvements and refinements within these areas. ● Work collaboratively with the Heads of IBD and AWM in matters falling within the scope of the role. 2.3. These responsibilities may be revised from time to time as deemed appropriate by business circumstances. 3. Duty & Obligation 3.1. You hereby undertake and agree with the Company that you will at all times during the continuance in force of this Employment observe, perform and covenant the following:- (i) will in all matters act faithfully to the Company and obey the result of discussion with the Executive Board of the Company, and in the absence of any such discussion in relation to any particular matter will act in such manner as you reasonably consider to be most beneficial to the Company’s interests; Page 2 of 6 (ii) will use your best endeavours to uphold the good name of the Company and at all times act in the best interest of the Company; (iii) will not make any wilful misleading or negligent representation or undertaking in respect of the services provided by the Company and will indemnify the Company for any loss or damages which the Company is liable to compensate to the prospects or any other loss incurred by the Company as a result of such representation or undertaking; (iv) will not incur any liability on behalf of the Company or pledge the Company’s credit or make any contract binding upon the Company without the Executive Board’s knowledge and consent in writing; (v) will promptly bring to the notice of the Executive Committee of the Company any information received by you which is likely to be of use or benefit to the Company; (vi) will not receive or accept any form of monetary gift from the prospects and its agent or any other persons in the similar nature without notifying the Executive Committee and the Company and obtaining the Company’s consent thereof; (vii) will not divulge any information in relation to the Company’s affairs or business or method of carrying on business. 3.2. Nature of Role – President, Business Development For the avoidance of doubt, this BD President role shall not fall under the scope of an “officer” under Rule 16a-1(f) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 nor shall it be part of the “executive officer” as per Rule 3b-7 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. Notwithstanding your non-officer role, you shall continue to be insured under CFOR’s D&O insurance policy for any claim arising from your service as President, Business Development of CFOR. 4. Entitlement 4.1. CFI SG is offering you a base salary of USD 13,000 per month (equivalent to SGD 16,640 at the pegged exchange rate of USD 1: SGD 1.28). 4.2. Your salary shall be subject to applicable taxes and statutory deductions or withholdings, where required by applicable law. The Company shall make the required employer Central Provident Fund (CPF) contributions and deduct the employee’s share of CPF contributions from your salary in accordance with the Central Provident Fund Act 1953 of Singapore, as amended from time to time. 4.3. Your salary shall be payable in arrears on the seventh (7 th ) day of the following calendar month and deposited into the bank account nominated by you. 4.4. You will be entitled to eighteen (18) days of annual leave per year. Annual leave must be planned, applied for in advance and approved in accordance with Company policy. Any carry-forward of unused annual leave shall be subject to the applicable carry-forward limit and utilisation deadline under Company policy. Page 3 of 6 4.5. You will be entitled to a one (1) month guaranteed bonus equivalent to one (1) month of your base salary, subject to standard tax deductions. 4.6. In addition to your base salary and guaranteed bonus, the Company may, at its discretion, grant you a performance-based bonus ranging from two (2) to twenty-four (24) months of your base salary, subject to your job performance assessed from both a company-wide and group-wide contribution perspective, the Company’s performance, and the Company’s applicable bonus cycle and approval. Any additional and/or performance bonus granted shall be entirely at the discretion of the Company and shall not constitute a guaranteed entitlement. 4.7. The stock grant provided in connection with your promotion in CFI Labuan effective 1 December 2025, originally valued at USD 200,000 upon completion of the first year of the promotion period, shall be calculated on a pro-rata basis up to 26 October 2026. As part of the Company’s acknowledgement of your performance, the Company shall grant you a discretionary bonus stock grant equivalent to 2,353 RSUs, to be completely vested by 30 November 2026. Effectively, you shall receive a total of 12-month stock grant for your tenure as CEO. Following your redesignation as BD President with effect from 27 October 2026, the applicable stock grant shall be valued at USD 150,000, subject to the applicable stock plan, corporate approvals, grant documentation, vesting requirements and other applicable terms and conditions. 4.8. This is on top of per-deal basis incentive allocated under a separate business development incentive agreement for front-end business development driven partner-level salaried employees, in relation to business leads sourcing/conversion at both investor/capital and investee/asset ends, be it on the buy-side asset management front or the sell-side investment banking front. 4.9. Based on your work performance, a stock grant shall be awarded by CapForce Inc., a listed company (OTCMKTS: CFOR) focused on a digital investment banking platform, under the separate business development incentive agreement stipulated under Clause 4.8 herein. 4.10. Under your employment terms with CFI Labuan commencing on 1 July 2025, you were entitled to a guaranteed minimum annual bonus equivalent to one (1) month of your monthly base salary of SGD 10,000 upon completion of your first year of service. This bonus has been paid in full. 4.11. You shall be covered under CapForce Inc.’s D&O insurance policy and shall continue to benefit from the existing indemnification arrangements, in each case in respect of all past and current roles held by you within CapForce Inc, CFI Labuan or CFI SG. Such coverage and indemnification shall extend to acts and omissions occurring during your tenure in each such capacity and shall survive the cessation of your employment or any such appointment, subject to the terms of the applicable insurance policy. 4.12. The change in your designation from an executive officer role to a non-executive officer role will be announced via a Form 8K disclosure. 5. Termination of Employment 5.1. Without prejudice to any other remedies the Company may have against you, the Company shall have the right at any time by giving three (3) months’ notice in writing to you to cease this Employment. 5.2. You may resign from your employment by giving to the Company three (3) months’ notice, provided that you shall continue to be liable to the Company for any obligations incurred prior to such cessation. Page 4 of 6 5.3. Notwithstanding Clause 5.1 above, the Company may terminate your employment with immediate effect in the event of serious misconduct, breach of fiduciary duty, or disqualification as a director. 5.4. Upon the termination of this employment, you undertake that you:- (i) shall return to the Company all documents obtained or accessed during this employment and shall not thereafter retain any of such documents in any form, including but not limited to documentation, devices or other media; (ii) shall not divulge any information in relation to the Company’s affairs or business or method of carrying on business; (iii) shall not continue to liaise, contact nor have any business dealing whatsoever in the same nature as the Company, either directly or indirectly, or through corporate entities or associates with any customer or client of the Company or its subsidiaries or any person or firm which has contacted or been contacted by the Company as a potential prospect; (iv) during the period of three (3) years after such cessation, shall not engage or participate directly or indirectly, or through any corporation, or associates in any business, enterprise, employment or appointment whether gainfully or not which is directly competitive with the Company; and (v) shall unconditionally return, as directed by the Company, all financial gain excluding its lawful entitlement made by you during your employment which is deemed to be held on trust for the Company. 5.5. In addition to Clause 5.4 above, both the Company and you agree that either party shall not disparage nor damage the interests, goodwill, reputations and/or businesses of the other party at all times. 5.6. With effect from the last date of this employment, both parties mutually release and discharge each other from all claims, liabilities and obligations arising out of or in connection with the your employment and termination thereof, whether known or unknown, except for any rights or obligations expressly preserved under this letter or which cannot lawfully be waived or released. 6. Confidentiality 6.1. You shall keep confidential any and all information whether oral or written relating to the business of the Company and be prohibited to disclose, use, make use or make available any documents of which you become aware during the term of this Employment to any person except as required, directed or permitted by the Executive Board of the CFOR. 6.2. You shall convey only the truthful, consistent and authorised documents to third parties including the companies or prospects as contained in any non-disclosure agreements. 6.3. You shall not directly or indirectly interfere with, circumvent or attempt to circumvent, avoid, by-pass or obviate the Company’s interest, or the interest or relationship between the Company and its clients, suppliers, service providers and any related parties via the connection of the Company. 6.4. The aforementioned clause in relation to confidentiality shall survive the cessation of this Employment, however caused. Page 5 of 6 7. Entire Agreement This Letter supersedes and replaces the previous letters issued to you in relation to your employment and appointments with the Company and its related entities and shall be governed by Singapore law. We appreciate your continued contribution to the Company and look forward to your continued leadership in your capacity as BD President. Yours faithfully, For and on behalf of CAPFORCE INC. /s/ Ethan Low Ethan Low Executive Director Page 6 of 6

title: CapForce Inc.
text: EX-10.2 4 capforceinc_ex10-2.htm EXHIBIT 10.2 Exhibit 10.2 Consulting Agreement This Consulting Agreement (the “ Agreement ”) is made and entered into as of October 27, 2026 (the “ Effective Date ”), by and between CapForce, Inc. , a Delaware corporation (the “ Company ”), and John Tan Honjian as the Chief Executive Officer (the “ CEO ”) of the Company. The Company and CEO may be referred to herein individually as “ Party ” or collectively, as “ Parties .” Recitals Whereas , the Company appointed CEO to serve as the Company’s Chief Executive Officer on top of his role of Chairman of the Board of Director; and Whereas , in consideration of the compensation to be paid by the Company to the CEO, the Parties now desire to enter into this Agreement to reflect, among other things, the agreement by the CEO to provide the services to the Company on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth herein. Agreement Now , Therefore , in consideration of the mutual covenants contained herein, the Parties hereto, intending to be legally bound, hereby agree as follows: 1. Engagement . Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Company hereby engages CEO to serve as the Company’s Chief Executive Officer, and the CEO hereby accepts such engagement. CEO shall have and perform such services and duties as shall from time to time, be delegated to the CEO by the Board of Directors of the Company. The CEO shall provide his services and duties to the Company in a good faith, professional, diligent manner and in a manner, it reasonably believes is in the best interests of the Company, and in accordance with applicable industry standards and applicable law. 2. Compensation . As CEO’s compensation for the performance of his obligations hereunder, CEO shall receive a monthly consultancy fee of $10,000 and on annual basis, a grant of restricted stock units by the Company representing a number of shares of common stock having a value equivalent to $150,000 as of the date of grant as part of his compensation package. 3. Independent Contractor . The Parties understand and agree that CEO is an independent contractor and not an employee of the Company. CEO shall not be considered an employee of the Company under any circumstances, irrespective of CEO’s classification under common law principles. It is understood that CEO shall perform the services contemplated in this Agreement according to CEO’s methods. The Company shall have no authority or right to direct or control CEO’s methods, and CEO shall only be subject to the control of the Company as to the results of the services performed. CEO has no authority to obligate the Company through contracts, agreements, or any other commitments, whether verbal or written, unless explicitly authorized in writing by the Company. In furtherance of the foregoing, CEO acknowledges and agrees that CEO will not be eligible to participate in any vacation, group medical or life insurance, disability, profit sharing or retirement benefits, retirement or 401(k) benefits, or any other fringe benefits or benefit plans of the Company, and the Company will not be responsible for withholding or paying any income, payroll or other foreign, federal, state or local taxes, making any insurance contributions, including for unemployment or disability or obtaining workers’ compensation insurance on your behalf. Any taxes imposed on CEO due to activities performed hereunder shall be the sole responsibility of CEO. 4. Intellectual Property . (a) All documents, work product, and other materials that are delivered under this Agreement (collectively, the “ Deliverables ”) and all other writings, technology, inventions, discoveries, processes, techniques, methods, ideas, concepts, research, proposals, and materials, and all other work product of any nature whatsoever, that are created, prepared, produced, authored, edited, modified, conceived, or reduced to practice in the course of performing the Services or other work performed in connection with the CEO’s services or this Agreement (collectively, and including the Deliverables, “ Work Product ”), and all patents, copyrights, trademarks (together with the goodwill symbolized thereby), trade secrets, know-how, and other confidential or proprietary information, and other intellectual property rights (collectively “ Intellectual Property Rights ”) therein, shall be owned exclusively by the Company. CEO acknowledges and agrees that any and all Work Product that may qualify as “work made for hire” as defined in the Copyright Act of 1976 (17 U.S.C. § 101) is hereby deemed “work made for hire” for the Company and all copyrights therein shall automatically and immediately vest in the Company. To the extent that any Work Product does not constitute “work made for hire,” CEO hereby irrevocably assigns to the Company and its successors and assigns, for no additional consideration, the CEO’s entire right, title, and interest in and to such Work Product and all Intellectual Property Rights therein, including the right to sue, counterclaim, and recover for all past, present, and future infringement, misappropriation, or dilution thereof. (b) Upon the reasonable request of the Company, during and after the Term, CEO shall promptly take such further actions, including execution and delivery of all appropriate instruments of conveyance, and provide such further cooperation, as may be reasonably necessary to assist the Company to apply for, prosecute, register, maintain, perfect, record, or enforce its rights in any Work Product and all Intellectual Property Rights therein. In the event the Company is unable, after reasonable effort, to obtain your signature on any such documents, CEO hereby irrevocably designates and appoints the Company as her agent and attorney-in-fact, to act for and on the CEO’s behalf solely to execute and file any such application or other document and do all other lawfully permitted acts to further the prosecution and issuance of patents, copyrights, or other intellectual property protection related to the Work Product with the same legal force and effect as if the CEO had executed them. The CEO agrees that this power of attorney is coupled with an interest. (c) As between the CEO and the Company, the Company is, and will remain, the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to any documents, specifications, data, know-how, methodologies, software, and other materials provided to the CEO by the Company (“ Company Materials ”), and all Intellectual Property Rights therein. The CEO shall have no right or license to reproduce or use any Company Materials except solely during the Term to the extent necessary to perform the CEO’s obligations under this Agreement. All other rights in and to the Company Materials are expressly reserved by the Company. The CEO shall have no right or license to use the Company’s trademarks, service marks, trade names, logos, symbols, or brand names. 5. Confidentiality . (a) The CEO understands that during the Term, the CEO may have access to unpublished and otherwise confidential information both of a technical and non-technical nature, relating to the business of the Company or any of its parents, subsidiaries, divisions, affiliates (collectively, “ Affiliated Entities ”), or clients, including without limitation any of their actual or anticipated business, research or development, any of their technology or the implementation or exploitation thereof, including without limitation information the CEO and others have collected, obtained or created, information pertaining to clients, accounts, vendors, prices, costs, materials, processes, codes, material results, technology, system designs, system specifications, materials of construction, trade secrets or equipment designs, including information disclosed to the Company or any of its Affiliated Entities by others under agreements to hold such information confidential (collectively, the “ Confidential Information ”). The CEO agrees to observe all policies and procedures of the Company and its Affiliated Entities concerning such Confidential Information. The CEO further agrees not to disclose or use, either during the Term or at any time thereafter, any Confidential Information for any purpose, including without limitation any competitive purpose, unless authorized 2 to do so by the Company in writing, except that the CEO may disclose and use such information in the good faith performance of the CEO’s duties for the Company. The CEO’s obligations under this Agreement will continue with respect to Confidential Information, whether or not this Agreement is terminated, until such information becomes generally available from public sources through no fault of the CEO or any representative of the CEO. Notwithstanding the foregoing, however, the CEO shall be permitted to disclose Confidential Information as may be required by a subpoena or other governmental order, provided that the CEO first notifies the Company of such subpoena, order or other requirement and such that the Company has the opportunity to obtain a protective order or other appropriate remedy. (b) During the Term, upon the Company’s request, or upon the termination of this Agreement for any reason, the CEO will promptly deliver to the Company all documents, records, files, notebooks, manuals, letters, notes, reports, client information and lists, cost and profit data, e-mail, apparatus, laptops, computers, smartphones, tablets or other PDAs, hardware, software, drawings, blueprints, and any other material of the Company or any of its Affiliated Entities or clients, including all materials pertaining to Confidential Information developed by the CEO or others, and all copies of such materials, whether of a technical, business or fiscal nature, whether on the hard drive of a laptop or desktop computer, in hard copy, disk or any other format, which are in the CEO’s possession, custody or control. 6. Nature of Agreement . This Agreement is personal to CEO, and CEO is not authorized to delegate any of the services to any subcontractors without the Company’s prior written consent. 7. Term and Termination . (a) This Agreement, along with CEO’s obligations hereunder, shall commence on the Effective Date and continue for a period of one (1) year thereafter (“ Term ”), unless terminated earlier as provided below. At the end of the Term, the Agreement shall be automatically renewed for additional periods unless the Company provides at least thirty (30) days written notice of termination, at its sole discretion. (b) The Company may terminate the Agreement at any time by giving no less than five (5) days’ prior written notice to the CEO. (c) Sections 3 through 15 shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement. Upon termination, CEO shall promptly deliver to Company all documents and other materials of any nature pertaining to the performance of its obligations hereunder. 8. Legal and Equitable Remedies . The CEO acknowledges that the Company would be irreparably injured by a violation of the covenants in Sections 5, 6 and 7 of this Agreement and agrees. Accordingly, in light of the foregoing and due to the personal and unique nature of the CEO’s services and because CEO may have access to and become acquainted with the Company’s proprietary or confidential information, Company shall have the right to enforce this Agreement, and any of its provisions, by injunction, specific performance, or other equitable relief without prejudice to any other rights and remedies that Company may have for in the event of a breach of this Agreement. 9. Governing Law ; Venue . This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed according to the laws of the State of Delaware, without regards to conflicts of laws rules. The CEO hereby expressly consents to the personal jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in the State of Delaware for any lawsuit filed there against the CEO by Company arising out or related to this Agreement. 10. Severability . If any provision of this Agreement is deemed by a court of competent jurisdiction to be unenforceable, that provision shall be severed and the remainder of this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect. 3 11. Waiver of Breach . The waiver by either the Company or the CEO of a breach of any provision of this Agreement shall not operate as or be deemed a waiver of any subsequent breach by either the Company or the CEO. Any waiver must be in writing. 12. Complete Understanding ; Modification . This Agreement, and all other documents mentioned herein, constitute the final, exclusive and complete understanding and agreement of the Parties hereto and supersedes all prior understandings and agreements. Any waiver, modification or amendment of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective only if in writing and signed by the Parties hereto. 13. Notices . Any notices required or permitted hereunder shall be delivered to the appropriate Party at the address listed on the signature page of the Agreement, or such other address as the Party shall specify in writing pursuant to this notice provision. Such notice shall be deemed given upon personal delivery to the appropriate address or three (3) days after the date of mailing if sent by certified or registered mail or electronic mail with confirmation of receipt. 14. Amendments . This Agreement may not be amended orally in any manner or in writing without the written consent of the Company and the CEO. No provision of this Agreement may be waived, delayed, modified, terminated or otherwise impaired without the prior written consent of the Company and the CEO. 15. Counterparts . This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts each of which shall be deemed an original, but all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. [Remainder of Page Intentionally Left Blank] 4 In Witness Whereof , the Parties hereto have executed this Agreement as of the date first written above. Company : CAPFORCE, INC. By: /s/ Ethan Low Name: Ethan Low Title: Executive Director CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER: /s/ John Tan Honjian Name: John Tan Honjian 5

text: EX-10.3 5 capforceinc_ex10-3.htm EXHIBIT 10.3 Exhibit 10.3 DIRECTOR AGREEMENT This Director Agreement (the “ Agreement ”) is made and entered into as of October 27, 2026 (the “ Effective Date ”), by and between CapForce, Inc. (the “ Company ”), and Mohd Azham Azudin (the “ Director ,” and together with the Company, the “ Parties ”). WHEREAS, the Director had previously served the Company as Chief Operating Officer of the Company (“COO”) and had been redesignated from the Company as COO effective October 27, 2026 following a personnel reshuffle in the Company. WHEREAS, the Company desires to continue to engage Director, and the Director is willing to continue such engagement, as a director of the Company upon the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth below, the Parties hereto hereby agrees as follows: 1. Engagement . Upon the terms and subject to the conditions of this Agreement, the Company hereby engages the Director to act as an executive director and provide services on the terms and conditions provided in this Agreement. The Director agrees to devote appropriate time and attention to the execution of the services to be provided by the Director hereunder, which shall include such services as the Company and the Director may reasonably agree (hereinafter the services to be provided by the Director hereunder are referred to as the “ Services ”). 2. Compensation . The Company shall pay the Director a fee of $3,000.00 per month pro-rated for a partial month during which the Director serves. The Company shall reimburse the Director for all reasonable business travel expenses previously authorized in writing by the Company and reasonably and necessarily incurred by the Director in the performance of his duties, responsibilities, and authorities hereunder. During the term of the Director’s engagement as a director of the Company, the Director shall not receive or be eligible to participate in the Company’s benefit programs in effect for the employees of the Company as in effect from time to time, on and after the Effective Date. In addition to the above, the Director shall remain eligible for the stock granted during his tenure as COO of the Company notwithstanding his redesignation before the completion if the vesting period of the stocks granted. 3. Term . Unless earlier terminated pursuant to Section 4 , the term of the Director’s engagement by the Company under this Agreement shall continue and terminate upon the Director ceasing to be a member of the Board of Directors of the Company (the “ Term ”). 4. Termination . The Term of this Agreement shall terminate effective upon the date of any of the following occurrences (such date, the “ Termination Date ”): (i) if at any time during the Term, the Company reasonably determines that the Director has been or will be unable, as a result of physical or mental illness or incapacity, to perform his duties hereunder for one year, the Term may be terminated by the Company upon written notice to the Director; (ii) either Party hereto may terminate the Term for any reason upon thirty (30) days written notice to the other Party; or (iii) the Term shall automatically terminate on the date of the Director’s death (such date being the Termination Date). All compensation earned as of such Termination Date shall be due and payable to the Director, which amount shall be paid by the Company to the Director within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date. 5. Restrictive Covenants . (a) The Director acknowledges and agrees that (i) the Director has a major responsibility for oversight of the operation, development and growth of the Company’s business; (ii) the Director’s work for the Company will bring him into close contact with Confidential Information (defined below) of the Company and its clients; and (iii) the agreements and covenants contained in this Section 5 are essential to protect the legitimate business interests of the Company and that the Company will not enter into this Agreement but for such agreements and covenants. (b) Non-solicitation of Employees of the Company, Directors of the Company or Customers or Suppliers of the Company . During the Term and for a three (3) year period thereafter (the “ Restricted Period ”), the Director shall not, directly or indirectly on behalf of any business, firm, corporation, partnership, person, proprietorship or other entity, incorporated or otherwise, and shall use his best efforts to cause each business, firm, corporation, partnership, person, proprietorship and other entity with which he is or shall become associated in any capacity not to, (i) solicit for employment, employ or otherwise engage any employee, officer, contractor or director of the Company, without the written consent of the Company, or (ii) except in connection with the performance of the Director’s duties hereunder and in accordance herewith, solicit, interfere with, endeavor to entice away from the Company or communicate with regarding the business of the Company any customer or supplier of the Company. The Director acknowledges and agrees in connection with the foregoing that the identities of the Company’s employees, officers, contractors, directors, customers, suppliers and clients and other information gained during his period of employment with the Company with respect thereto is Confidential Information (as more fully defined in Section 5(c) below) of the Company. (c) Confidentiality . During the Restricted Period and at all times thereafter, the Director agrees and acknowledges that the Confidential Information (as defined below) of the Company is valuable, special and unique to its business; that such business depends on such Confidential Information; and that the Company wishes to protect such Confidential Information by keeping it confidential for the exclusive use and benefit of the Company. The Director further acknowledges that any use by him of the Confidential Information other than in strict accordance with the terms of this Agreement would be wrongful and would cause the Company irreparable injury. Based upon the foregoing, with respect to such Confidential Information, the Director agrees: (i) to keep any and all Confidential Information in trust for the sole use and benefit of the Company; (ii) except as required by applicable law or as required in furtherance of the business of the Company in accordance with the terms hereof, not to use or disclose or reproduce, directly or indirectly, any Confidential Information of the Company; (iii) to take all steps necessary or reasonably requested by the Company to ensure that all Confidential Information is kept confidential for the sole use and benefit of the Company; and (iv) in the event the Director’s service as a director with the Company terminates for any reason whatsoever or at any time that the Company may in writing request, to deliver promptly to the Company all materials constituting Confidential Information (including all written, graphic, facsimile, encoded or recorded copies or duplicates thereof or notes regarding the same) of the Company that are in his possession or under his control without making or retaining any written graphic, facsimile, encoded or recorded copy or extract from such materials. “ Confidential Information ” means any and all information developed by or for or possessed by the Company prior to or during the Term that is (A) not generally known in any industry in which the Company does business as of the date hereof or during the Term or (B) not publicly available (including for this purpose information that is publicly available because of a breach by the Director of the provisions hereof). Confidential Information includes, but is not limited to, the information identified in this Section 5(c ) (including, without limitation, personnel records and applications, employment and other Director agreements, medical records, Director appraisals, reviews and evaluations, general wage and salary rates and individual salaries and bonuses and plans and records relating thereto, numbers of Directors in departments and divisions, Director benefit plans and incentive plans), and any and all other information developed by or for or possessed by the Company concerning information technology, marketing and sales methods, concepts, materials, products, processes, procedures, formulae, compounds, formulations, models, innovations, discoveries, improvements, inventions, protocols, computer programs, records, data, know-how, techniques, designs, machinery, devices, research and development projects, data, preparations, business forms, strategies, plans for development of products, services or expansion into new areas or markets, internal operations, product price lists, forecasts, projections, financial information (including the revenues, costs or profits associated with the products of the Company) and any other trade secrets and proprietary information of any type owned by or pertaining to the Company, together with all written, graphic, facsimile, encoded, recorded and other materials relating to all or any part of the same. 2 (d) Noncompetition, etc . During the Restricted Period and any extension thereof, the Director shall not, directly or indirectly, engage in or be associated with, whether as a director, officer, employee, agent, Director, shareholder, partner, owner, independent contractor or otherwise, any business, firm, corporation, partnership, person, proprietorship or other entity, incorporated or otherwise (other than the Company), which is conducting, or plans to conduct, any business which competes with or will compete with, in the United States, (i) the business of the Company as constituted during the Term, or (ii) the products of the Company manufactured, sold or under development by the Company during the Term; provided, however, nothing herein shall prohibit the Director from being a shareholder in any entity that competes with the Company so long as the Director does not control such entity and does not hold more than a five percent (5%) equity interest therein. (e) Compliance With Laws . In performing the Director’s duties hereunder, the Director agrees to comply with all applicable governmental laws, rules and regulations and all applicable policies and procedures of the Company. (f) Remedies . The Director acknowledges that the Company would be irreparably injured by a violation of the covenants contained in this Section 5 and agrees that the Company shall be entitled to an injunction restraining the Director from any actual or threatened breach of the covenants contained in Section 5 , or to any other appropriate equitable remedy without bond or other security being required. Any such relief shall be in addition to and not in lieu of any appropriate relief in the way of monetary damages that the parties may seek in arbitration. Director agrees that if the duration or the scope of or any business activity covered by any provision of this Section 5 is in excess of what is determined to be valid and enforceable under applicable law, such provision shall be construed to cover only that duration, scope or activity that is determined to be valid and enforceable. Director hereby acknowledges that this Section 5 shall be given the construction that renders its provisions valid and enforceable to the maximum extent, not exceeding its express terms, possible under applicable law. 6. Representations, Warranties and Covenants of the Director . The Director hereby represents and warrants to the Company as follows: (a) Capacity . The Director has full legal capacity to enter into and perform the Director’s obligations under this Agreement; (b) No Conflict . The execution, delivery and performance by the Director of this Agreement will not conflict with or result in a breach of any of the terms, conditions or provisions of, or constitute (with due notice or lapse of time or both) a default under, any agreement or instrument to which the Director is a party or by which he is bound. The Director is not subject to any agreement restricting his ability to enter into this Agreement and fully carry out his duties and responsibilities hereunder; and (c) Execution and Enforceability . This Agreement has been duly executed and delivered by the Director and constitutes a binding agreement enforceable against Director in accordance with its terms. 7. Indemnification . The Company shall indemnify the Director and each of his agents against any loss, liability, claim, damage, or expense arising from the actions or inactions of the Company (or any of its officers and directors), including, but not limited to, any and all out of pocket expense and reasonable attorneys’ fees whatsoever reasonably incurred in investigating, preparing, or defending against any litigation, commenced or threatened, or any third party claim whatsoever), to which the Director may become subject arising out of or based on any actions or inactions or operations of the Company (or any of its officers and directors), to the fullest extent permitted by the Delaware General Corporation Law. Such indemnification does not include any claims resulting from the gross negligence, willful misconduct or bad faith of the Director. 8. Waiver of Breach . The waiver by either the Company or the Director of a breach of any provision of this Agreement shall not operate as or be deemed a waiver of any subsequent breach by either the Company or the Director. Any waiver must be in writing. 3 9. Notice . All notices and other communications hereunder shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been given when delivered by hand or courier service, or mailed by first-class certified mail, postage prepaid and return receipt requested, addressed as follows: (a) to the Director, at the address on file with the Company. (b) to the Company addressed as follows: CapForce, Inc . 23219 Stringtown Road, Suite 300 Clarksburg, MD 20871 or, in each case, at such other address as may from time to time be specified to the other party in a notice similarly given. 10. Amendment . This Agreement may not be amended orally in any manner or in writing without the written consent of the Company and the Director. No provision of this Agreement may be waived, delayed, modified, terminated or otherwise impaired without the prior written consent of the Company and the Director. 11. Entire Agreement . This Agreement embodies the entire agreement and understanding of the parties hereto in respect of the Director’s directorship with the Company contemplated by this Agreement and supersedes all prior agreements, arrangements and understandings, oral or written, express or implied, between the parties with respect to such agreement. Sections 5 through 17 of this Agreement shall survive the termination of this Agreement. 12. Governing Law . The provisions of this Agreement shall be construed in accordance with the internal laws of Malaysia, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. 13. Expenses . Except as otherwise provided herein, all costs and expenses (including attorneys’ fees) incurred in connection with the negotiation and preparation of, or any claim, dispute or litigation pertaining to, this Agreement shall be paid by the party incurring such expenses. 14. Assignment; Successors and Assigns, etc . This Agreement is a personal contract and Director may not sell, transfer, assign, pledge or hypothecate his rights, interests and obligations hereunder. Except as otherwise herein expressly provided, this Agreement shall be binding upon and shall inure to the benefit of Director and his personal representatives and shall inure to the benefit of and be binding upon the Company and its successors and assigns, except that the Company may not assign this Agreement without Director’s prior written consent, except to an acquirer of all or substantially all of the assets of the Company. 15. Arbitration . All disputes and disagreements arising from, relating to, or otherwise connected with this Agreement, the breach of this Agreement, the enforcement, interpretation or validity of this Agreement, or the directorship relationship (including any wage claim, claim for wrongful termination, or any claim based upon any statute, regulation, or law, including those dealing with discrimination or retaliation, sexual harassment, civil rights, age, or disability) that the Company may have against Director or that Director may have against the Company, including the determination of the scope or applicability of this Agreement to arbitrate, shall be settled by arbitration administered by the Judicial Arbitration and Mediation Services (“ JAMS ”). Arbitration shall take place in Wilmington, DE and shall be conducted before a single arbitrator selected by and in accordance with the rules and procedures of JAMS. The decision of the arbitrator shall be final and binding on the parties. Judgment on any award may be entered in any court having competent jurisdiction, and application may be made to such court for a judicial acceptance of the award and an order of enforcement, as the case may be. The expenses of the arbitration (including any arbitrator fees) shall be borne equally by the Director and the Company. Each of the parties shall bear the fees and expenses of its own legal counsel. 4 16. Enforceability . If any portion or provision of this Agreement (including, without limitation, any portion or provision of any section of this Agreement) shall to any extent be declared illegal or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, then the remainder of this Agreement, or the application of such portion or provision in circumstances other than those as to which it is so declared illegal or unenforceable, shall not be affected thereby, and each portion and provision of this Agreement shall be valid and enforceable to the fullest extent permitted by law. 17. Withholding Taxes . The Company shall deduct any foreign, federal, state or local withholding or other taxes from any payments to be made by the Company hereunder in such amounts which the Company reasonably determines are required to be deducted under applicable law. 18. Counterparts; Construction . This Agreement may be executed in multiple counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall be considered one and the same agreement and shall become effective when one or more counterparts have been signed by each of the parties and delivered to the other party. Facsimile or .pdf signatures shall have the same force and effect as original signatures. This Agreement shall not be construed more strictly against one Party than the other, merely by virtue of the fact that it may have been prepared by counsel for one of the Parties, it being recognized that both Company and Director have contributed substantially and materially to the negotiation and preparation of this Agreement. In construing this Agreement, the singular shall include the plural and the plural shall include the singular, and the use of any gender shall include every other and all genders. [ remainder of page intentionally left blank ] 5 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Director and the Company have executed this Agreement as of the date first above written. /s/ Mohd Azham Azudin Mohd Azham Azudin CapForce, Inc. text: EX-10.4 6 capforceinc_ex10-4.htm EXHIBIT 10.4 Exhibit 10.4 Date: 27 October 2026 PRIVATE & CONFIDENTIAL TAN THENG WEI Dear Tan Theng Wei, RE: LETTER OF OFFER CapForce Inc. (the “ CFOR ”) is pleased to offer TAN THENG WEI the appointment as Chief Operating Officer (“ COO ”) of the Company on a consultancy basis, in connection with and alongside your full-time employment as a Director of CapForce International (SG) Pte. Ltd. (“ CFI SG ”). CFOR and CFI SG shall be collectively referred to as the “ Company ”. The employment is offered on the following terms and conditions: 1. Terms of Employment 1.1. You will be employed by CFI SG while formally appointed to serve the Company as the COO and CFI SG as its director. Your direct employment relationship, payroll administration, and contractual benefits shall exist solely and exclusively with CFI SG. 1.2. Your employment shall commence with effect from 27 October 2026 and is subject to a six (6) months probationary period. This period of time allows you and the Company to determine if the position is suitable for you. The Company reserves the right to revise the terms and conditions of your employment from time to time. 1.3. Subject to satisfactory performance and conduct, your employment may be confirmed upon successful completion of the six (6) months probationary period. 1.4. Your ordinary hours of work will be from Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 18:00. You are required to work at the designated workplace for three (3) days per week, with the remaining two (2) days under a remote working arrangement. You may be requested to work outside your normal working hours, including weekends and public holidays, where reasonably necessary to fulfil your duties and responsibilities. 2. Role/Duties Oversee the day-to-day operations of the Company and ensure effective execution of its business activities and operational priorities. 2.1. Translate the Company’s business strategy and objectives into operational plans and ensure effective execution across relevant functions. 2.2. Lead cross-functional coordination and ensure that teams and business functions are aligned in the execution of the Company’s operational priorities. 2.3. Establish and monitor operational processes, procedures and performance standards to support efficient and effective business operations. 2.4. Monitor operational performance and key business metrics, identify areas for improvement and implement appropriate measures to improve efficiency, productivity and execution. 2.5. Oversee the allocation and utilisation of operational resources to support the Company’s business requirements. 2.6. Identify and monitor operational risks and implement appropriate measures to support business continuity and effective risk management. 2.7. Establish and maintain appropriate operational controls, policies and procedures to support effective governance and execution. 2.8. Oversee the performance of teams and functions under the COO’s responsibility and provide direction and support where required. 2.9. Work closely with the CEO and senior management on the implementation and execution of strategic initiatives and key business priorities. 2.10. Drive continuous improvement across business operations and recommend measures to improve overall organisational effectiveness. 2.11. Support the Company’s strategic and operational initiatives and other matters as assigned by the Executive Board. 2.12. Support the CEO on transaction-related business development and advisory activities and provide senior-level advisory and commercial input on relevant transaction opportunities. 2.13. As a Director of CFI SG, you shall perform such duties and responsibilities as may be required of you in accordance with applicable laws, the constitution of CFI SG, and the directions and resolutions of the Executive Board and/or Executive Committee. These responsibilities may be revised from time to time as deemed appropriate by business circumstances. 3. Duty & Obligation 3.1. You hereby undertake and agree with the Company that you will at all times during the continuance in force of this Employment observe, perform and covenant the following:- (i) will in all matters act faithfully to the Company and obey the result of discussion with the Executive Board of the Company, and in the absence of any such discussion in relation to any particular matter will act in such manner as you reasonably consider to be most beneficial to the Company’s interests; (ii) will use your best endeavours to uphold the good name of the Company and at all times act in the best interest of the Company; (iii) will not make any wilful misleading or negligent representation or undertaking in respect of the services provided by the Company and will indemnify the Company for any loss or damages which the Company is liable to compensate to the prospects or any other loss incurred by the Company as a result of such representation or undertaking; Page 2 of 5 (iv) will not incur any liability on behalf of the Company or pledge the Company’s credit or make any contract binding upon the Company without the Executive Board’s knowledge and consent in writing; (v) will promptly bring to the notice of the Executive Committee of the Company any information received by you which is likely to be of use or benefit to the Company; (vi) will not receive or accept any form of monetary gift from the prospects and its agent or any other persons in the similar nature without notifying the Executive Committee and the Company and obtaining the Company’s consent thereof; (vii) will not divulge any information in relation to the Company’s affairs or business or method of carrying on business. 4. Entitlement 4.1. CFI SG is offering you a base salary of USD 9,000 per month. 4.2. Your salary shall be subject to applicable taxes and statutory deductions or withholdings, where required by applicable law. 4.3. Your salary shall be payable in arrears on the seventh (7 th ) day of the following calendar month and deposited into the bank account nominated by you. 4.4. You will be entitled to eighteen (18) days of annual leave per year. Annual leave must be planned, applied for in advance and approved in accordance with Company policy. Any carry-forward of unused annual leave shall be subject to the applicable carry-forward limit and utilisation deadline under Company policy. 4.5. For the first year of your appointment, you will be eligible for an annual stock grant with a fixed value of USD 120,000, subject to the applicable stock plan, relevant corporate approvals, grant documentation, vesting requirements and other applicable terms and conditions. 4.6. In addition to your base salary, the Company may, at its discretion, grant you a performance-based bonus, subject to your job performance, the Company’s performance, completion of one (1) full year of service, and the Company’s applicable bonus cycle and approval. Any bonus granted shall be entirely at the discretion of the Company and shall not constitute a guaranteed entitlement. 5. Termination of Employment 5.1. Without prejudice to any other remedies the Company may have against you, the Company shall have the right at any time by giving three (3) months’ notice in writing to you to cease this Employment. 5.2. You may resign from your employment by giving to the Company three (3) months’ notice, provided that you shall continue to be liable to the Company for any obligations incurred prior to such cessation. 5.3. Notwithstanding Clause 5.1 above, the Company may terminate your employment with immediate effect in the event of serious misconduct, breach of fiduciary duty, or disqualification as a director. 5.4. Upon the termination of this employment, you undertake that you:- (i) shall return to the Company all documents obtained or accessed during this employment and shall not thereafter retain any of such documents in any form, including but not limited to documentation, devices or other media; Page 3 of 5 (ii) shall not divulge any information in relation to the Company’s affairs or business or method of carrying on business; (iii) shall not continue to liaise, contact nor have any business dealing whatsoever in the same nature as the Company, either directly or indirectly, or through corporate entities or associates with any customer or client of the Company or its subsidiaries or any person or firm which has contacted or been contacted by the Company as a potential prospect; (iv) during the period of three (3) years after such cessation, shall not engage or participate directly or indirectly, or through any corporation, or associates in any business, enterprise, employment or appointment whether gainfully or not which is directly competitive with the Company; (v) shall not disparage nor damage the interests, goodwill, reputations and businesses of the Company at all times; (vi) shall unconditionally return, as directed by the Company, all financial gain excluding its lawful entitlement made by you during your employment which is deemed to be held on trust for the Company. 6. Confidentiality 6.1. You shall keep confidential any and all information whether oral or written relating to the business of the Company and be prohibited to disclose, use, make use or make available any documents of which you become aware during the term of this Employment to any person except as required, directed or permitted by the Executive Board of the Company. 6.2. You shall convey only the truthful, consistent and authorised documents to third parties including the companies or prospects as contained in any non-disclosure agreements. 6.3. You shall not directly or indirectly interfere with, circumvent or attempt to circumvent, avoid, by-pass or obviate the Company’s interest, or the interest or relationship between the Company and its clients, suppliers, service providers and any related parties via the connection of the Company. 6.4. The aforementioned clause in relation to confidentiality shall survive the cessation of this Employment, however caused. 7. Entire Agreement This Letter supersedes and replaces the previous letters issued to you in relation to your employment and appointments with the Company and its related entities. We look forward to your outstanding performance. Yours faithfully, For and on behalf of CAPFORCE INC. /s/ Ethan Low Ethan Low Executive Director Page 4 of 5 ACKNOWLEDGEMENT AND ACCEPTANCE FORM I, TAN THENG WEI hereby confirm my acceptance of this Letter of Offer for the position of Chief Operating Officer. I hereby declare that I have fully understood the content herein and agreed to be bound by the said content.
