text: EX-10.1 2 karx_ex101.htm INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR SERVICES AGREEMENT karx_ex101.htm EXHIBIT 10.1 Certain personal information has been omitted from this exhibit pursuant to Item 601(a)(6) of Regulation S-K. Omitted information is marked [***] INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR SERVICES AGREEMENT This Independent Contractor Services Agreement (the “ Con tract ”) is entered into on the 1st of November (the “ Effective Date ”) by and between: KA RBON-X CORP. , a Nevada corporation, with corporate registry number NV20171590185 and its registered address at 6575 West Loop South, Suite 500 Bellaire, TX 77401 , acting through its Board of Directors (hereinafter “ KARBON-X ” or the “ CLIENT ”); and S HN ADVISORY LLC , a Texas limited liability company (Texas Secretary of State File No. 6000038886) with its principal place of business at [***] , with mailing address at [***] and U.S. Taxpayer Identification Number [***] , acting on its own behalf and represented herein by Samuel Hamilton Nelson, its sole member (the “ Key Indi vidual ”) (hereinafter the “ CO NTRACTOR ”). KARBON-X and the CONTRACTOR are referred to individually as a “ Party ” and collectively as the “ Parties ”. RECITALS W HEREAS KARBON-X is an international company that develops environmental financing solutions for sustainable energy, landfill and forestry projects and environmental markets in Europe, North America, Asia, Africa and Latin America. KARBON-X offers consulting services for climate change and sustainability solutions, including the measurement of carbon, plastic and water footprint, the development of greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction projects and the purchase and sale of Environmental Credits (ECs) generated by those projects; W HEREAS the CONTRACTOR is an independent consulting company engaged in the independent trade, occupation, profession or business of financial reporting, SEC reporting and accounting advisory services, offers such services to the public and to clients other than KARBON-X, and has the skills, licences, equipment and resources necessary to perform the Services; W HEREAS the board of directors of KARBON-X (the “Board”) has appointed, or intends to appoint, Samuel Hamilton Nelson as Chief Financial Officer of KARBON-X, and the Parties intend that the office is held in connection with, and incidental to, the Services provided by the CONTRACTOR as an independent contractor; W HEREAS the CONTRACTOR accepted the proposal communicated by KARBON-X in October 2026 provided that, in the event of any inconsistency, this Contract shall prevail over the Proposal; 1 NOW, THEREFORE , in consideration of the recitals and the mutual covenants set forth in this Contract, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree to the following terms and conditions: CLAUSES 1. D EFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION 1.1. In this Contract: (a) “ Affili ate ” means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by or is under common control with KARBON-X, including Karbon-X USA Corp.; (b) “ Busin ess Day ” means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or United States federal public holiday; (c) “ Conf idential Information ” means all non-public information, in any form, disclosed by or on behalf of KARBON-X or its Affiliates, or obtained by the CONTRACTOR in performing the Services, including information on projects, Environmental Credits, pricing, counterparties, off takers, investors, methodologies, MRV data, financial information, know-how, trade secrets and the terms of this Contract; (d) “ D eliverables ” means the Products, reports, data, materials and other work product to be delivered under Clauses 4 and 5 and Schedule A; (e) “ Dispu te ” has the meaning given in Clause 23.1; (f) “ In tellectual Property ” means all patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, database rights, know-how, methodologies, software and all other intellectual property rights anywhere in the world, whether registered or not; (g) “ KA RBON-X Parties ” means KARBON-X, its Affiliates and their respective directors, officers, employees, agents, successors and assigns; and (h) “ S ervices ” means the services described in Clause 4 and Schedule A. 1.2. Headings are for convenience only. “Including” means “including without limitation”. No rule of construction shall apply to the disadvantage of a Party on the basis that such Party prepared this Contract or any part of it. 2 2. PURPOSE The purpose of this Contract is for the CONTRACTOR, acting as an independent contractor, to provide financial reporting, SEC reporting and internal control over financial reporting services to KARBON-X and its Affiliates, including through the Key Individual holding the Office, in accordance with the specifications set out in Schedule A. 3. TERM This Contract shall remain in force for twelve (12) months from the Effective Date (the “ Term ”), unless terminated earlier under Clause 19. This Contract renews automatically for successive twelve (12)-month periods unless either Party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current Term. Any change to the Fee for a renewal period requires the approval of the Board under the Fee Letter. 4. SERVICES AND OBLIGATIONS OF THE CONTRACTOR 4.1. The CONTRACTOR shall provide the following Services to KARBON-X, as itemized in Schedule A: (a) Financial reporting and SEC filings: preparation of the monthly consolidated close, quarterly and annual financial statements and Forms 10-Q, 10-K and 8-K and other SEC filings, and their signature and certification by the Key Individual where required under Clause 11.9; (b) In ternal control over financial reporting: documentation, testing calendar and deficiency reporting for internal control over financial reporting; (c) Audi t coordination: coordination of the PCAOB audit and quarterly reviews with the external auditors in accordance with the audit timetable; (d) Technical accounting and financing reporting: technical accounting memoranda as transactions arise, and financing and lender reporting as required by the financing agreements; 4.2. The CONTRACTOR shall ensure that the total value described in this Contract is complete and that no additional costs of any kind will be added without the express written consent of KARBON-X. 4.3. The CONTRACTOR is responsible for providing the Services and complying with the obligations set forth in this Contract with the skill, care and diligence of a qualified professional, in compliance with applicable law and the specifications set out in Schedule A. 4.4. The CONTRACTOR will provide the Services from the locations it chooses and, where necessary to develop this Contract’s purpose, at such other places as are reasonably required. 4.5. The CONTRACTOR shall accept, comply with and abide by, in its entirety, the KARBON-X Suppliers Code of Conduct referred to in Clause 12 and attached as Annex 1, or any other code that replaces it, reject all behavior contrary to it and report any such behavior in accordance with its provisions. 3 4.6. The CONTRACTOR shall obtain and maintain, at its own cost, all licences, permits, registrations, equipment, tools and personnel necessary to perform the Services. 4.7. Any other services that the Parties agree upon must be set out in writing, signed by both Parties and annexed to this Contract. 5. PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES The CONTRACTOR will deliver the following Products, in accordance with the delivery schedule set out in Schedule A: (a) a monthly consolidated close package and cash forecast, delivered by the tenth (10th) Business Day of each month; (b) filing-ready quarterly financial statements and Form 10-Q by the applicable SEC filing deadline (including any Rule 12b-25 extension), filing-ready annual financial statements and Form 10-K by the applicable SEC filing deadline (including any Rule 12b-25 extension), other SEC filings within statutory deadlines, a quarterly ICFR report, and technical accounting memoranda and lender reports as required. 6. OBLIGATIONS OF KARBON-X 6.1. Provide the information and documentation reasonably requested by the CONTRACTOR and necessary to enable it to perform the Services. 6.2. Pay the Fee in accordance with Clause 7, subject to compliance with the requirements established for that purpose. 6.3. Make reasonable efforts to ensure timely attention to the concerns raised by the CONTRACTOR in the execution of this Contract. 6.4. Attend and help organise the meetings reasonably necessary for the CONTRACTOR to perform the Services. 6.5. The Parties agree that the Services may be provided to KARBON-X or to any of its KARBON-X Parties, as specified in Schedule A. 7. FEE AND PAYMENT 7.1. In consideration for the Services, KARBON-X will pay the CONTRACTOR a monthly retainer and any other fees set out in a fee letter approved by the Board and signed by both Parties (the “Fee Letter”) (together, the “Fee”). The monthly retainer is payable for each month of the Term in which the CONTRACTOR has performed the Services in accordance with this Contract, subject to KARBON-X’s right to dispute amounts in good faith under Clause 7.5. Any failure to perform to the extent resulting from KARBON-X, its auditors or other third parties outside the CONTRACTOR’s reasonable control shall not affect payment. The monthly retainer for each calendar month is payable on the last Business Day of that month. The Parties may review the Fee from time to time, and KARBON-X may, in its discretion, pay the CONTRACTOR an additional fee in recognition of results delivered under this Contract, as set out in the Fee Letter or a written amendment approved by the Board. No payment is conditioned on the content of any financial statement, filing or certification, or on the Key Individual’s exercise of independent professional judgment. 4 7.2. Payment will be made by wire or ACH transfer to an account held in the name of the CONTRACTOR, as designated by the CONTRACTOR in writing or stated on its invoices and verified under KARBON-X’s payment procedures. Any change to that account takes effect only after KARBON-X has verified it. 7.3. Payments may be made by KARBON-X or by Karbon-X USA Corp. as paying agent, in United States Dollars. Payment by a paying agent does not make it a party to this Contract. 7.4. The monthly retainer shall be paid on the last Business Day of the month to which it relates. A failure by KARBON-X to pay any amount when due shall not constitute an event of default and shall not entitle the CONTRACTOR to suspend the Services, terminate this Contract or claim damages, unless KARBON-X fails to pay such amount in full within seven (7) Business Days after receipt of written notice (including email) from the CONTRACTOR identifying the overdue amount. Any other amount invoiced under this Contract shall be paid within fifteen (15) days after receipt by KARBON-X of a conforming invoice. Amounts disputed in good faith shall not be considered overdue for the purposes of this Clause. 7.5. KARBON-X may withhold any invoiced amount that it disputes in good faith, by notifying the CONTRACTOR in writing of the reasons within five (5) Business Days after receipt of the relevant invoice, and shall pay the undisputed portion. Any invoiced amount, and any Deliverable to which it relates, not disputed within that period shall be deemed accepted. KARBON-X may set off against any amount payable to the CONTRACTOR any undisputed amount owed by the CONTRACTOR to KARBON-X under this Contract. 7.6. To the extent permitted by applicable law, the CONTRACTOR shall invoice any amount it claims under this Contract within one hundred and eighty (180) days after the end of the month in which the relevant Services were performed, failing which such amount shall be deemed waived. 5 7.7. Nothing that the Parties have not agreed in writing will be deemed agreed. 7.8. Equity Awards. The following shall apply to stock options and other equity awards over shares of Karbon-X Corp. (the “ Issu e r ”): (a) Plan governs. Any stock option or other equity award granted, or to be granted, to the CONTRACTOR or the Key Individual under the Equity Incentive Plan of the Issuer (the “ Plan ”) (each, an “ Equity Award ”) is governed exclusively by the Plan, the applicable award agreement and the resolutions of the Issuer’s board of directors or its competent committee (the “ Bo ard ”). In the event of any conflict, the Plan and the award agreement shall prevail over this Contract. (b) Con tinued vesting. Equity Awards granted before the Effective Date in connection with any prior employment or service relationship between the CONTRACTOR or the Key Individual and any KARBON-X Party (including any stock options granted under the offer letter dated January 12, 2026 ) shall, subject to the Plan and to Board approval, continue to vest in accordance with their existing vesting schedule, and shall retain their existing exercise price, expiration date and other terms, for so long as the CONTRACTOR continues to provide the Services under this Contract without interruption. The Parties intend that the change of status from employee to independent contractor shall not, by itself, constitute a termination or interruption of continuous service under the Plan. KARBON-X shall procure that the Board adopts, before the Effective Date, any resolution required to give effect to this paragraph. (c) Tax treatment. The CONTRACTOR acknowledges that: (i) any Equity Award granted as an incentive stock option will cease to qualify as such, and will be treated as a non- qualified stock option, if it is not exercised within three (3) months after the termination of employment, in accordance with Section 422 of the Internal Revenue Code; and (ii) all taxes arising from the grant, vesting, exercise or disposition of Equity Awards after the Effective Date are the sole responsibility of the CONTRACTOR or the Key Individual under Clause 10.2. No KARBON-X Party makes any representation as to the tax treatment of the Equity Awards, and the CONTRACTOR shall obtain its own tax advice. (d) S ecurities laws and policies. The grant, vesting, exercise and transfer of Equity Awards are subject to applicable securities laws, including the availability of a registration statement or an exemption for awards to consultants, and to the Issuer’s insider trading policy, blackout periods and any clawback or recoupment policy adopted by the Issuer or required by law. The CONTRACTOR shall procure that the Key Individual complies with them. 6 (e) Termination. Vesting shall cease on the earlier of (i) the date on which this Contract terminates for any reason, and (ii) the date on which the Key Individual ceases to perform the Services personally. Unvested Equity Awards shall then be forfeited without compensation, and vested Equity Awards may be exercised only within the post-termination exercise period set out in the Plan or the award agreement. If this Contract is terminated under Clause 19.1(d) or 19.1(e), or if the CONTRACTOR breaches Clause 13, 15 or 21, all unvested Equity Awards shall be forfeited, and vested Equity Awards shall be forfeited only in the case of fraud or wilful misconduct, to the extent permitted by the Plan and applicable law. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing in this Clause shall operate to forfeit, accelerate the expiration of, or otherwise adversely modify any Equity Award except as expressly permitted under the applicable Plan and award agreement. (f) No other rights. Equity Awards do not form part of the Fee and do not constitute compensation for Services rendered in any particular period. Any new Equity Award is discretionary and does not create any right to future awards. Neither the CONTRACTOR nor the Key Individual shall be entitled to any compensation or damages for the loss, forfeiture or reduction in value of any Equity Award, including upon termination of this Contract for any reason. (g) No employment relationship. Participation in the Plan is as a non-employee service provider. It does not create any employment relationship with any KARBON-X Party and does not affect Clause 11. 8. REPORTING 8.1. The CONTRACTOR shall report on the progress and results of the Services to the Chief Executive Officer of KARBON-X (the “Supervisor”) and to the Board (and, for matters within its remit, the Audit Committee). Reporting under this Clause relates to results and does not give any person the right to direct the manner in which the Services are performed. 8.2. The role of the Supervisor is limited to receiving reports on results. SCHEDULE 1 FEE LETTER KARBON-X CORP. 6575 West Loop South, Suite 500 Bellaire, TX 77401 Date: 30 of October 2026 To: SHN Advisory LLC [***] Attention: Samuel Hamilton Nelson Subject: Fee Letter under Clause 7.1 of the Independent Contractor Services Agreement dated 1st of November 2026 (the “Contract”) Dear Mr. Nelson, 1. Fee Letter. This letter is the Fee Letter referred to in Clause 7.1 of the Contract between Karbon- X Corp. (“ K ARBON-X ”) and SHN Advisory LLC (the “ CONTRACTOR ”). It has been approved by the Board of Directors of KARBON-X by unanimous written consent dated The 30th of October. Capitalized terms not defined in this letter have the meaning given to them in the Contract. 2. Monthly retainer. The monthly retainer payable to the CONTRACTOR under Clause 7.1 of the Contract is: (a) US$ 22,393.51 per month (US$ 268,722.08 per year); and (b) US$ 25,726.84 per month from the month after KARBON-X first receives, after the Effective Date, aggregate new cash proceeds of at least US$ 2,000,000 from equity, convertible securities or debt with a maturity of more than twelve (12) months. The monthly retainer is payable for each month of the Term in which the CONTRACTOR has performed the Services in accordance with the Contract, subject to KARBON-X’s right to dispute amounts in good faith under Clause 7.5. The CONTRACTOR shall invoice it in accordance with Clause 9.1, and KARBON-X shall pay it on the last Business Day of the month to which it relates, in accordance with Clause 7.4, by wire or ACH transfer to the account of the CONTRACTOR stated in Clause 7.2. KARBON-X may disclose this letter and file it with the Securities and Exchange Commission, as provided in Clause 13.8 of the Contract. 9. Contract. This letter forms part of the Contract and is governed by Clauses 22 and 23 of the Contract. In the event of any conflict as to the amount of the Fee, this letter prevails; in all other respects, the Contract prevails. Yours faithfully, KARBON-X CORP. text: EX-10.4 5 d141597dex104.htm EX-10.4 EX-10.4 Exhibit 10.4 FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE FOX CORPORATION 2019 SHAREHOLDER ALIGNMENT PLAN This First Amendment (this “ Amendment ”) to the Fox Corporation 2019 Shareholder Alignment Plan (the “ Plan ”) is adopted by the Board of Directors (the “ Board ”) of Fox Corporation, a Delaware corporation (the “ Company ”), effective as of the Effective Time. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Amendment have the meanings given to them in the Plan. RECITALS WHEREAS , the Company, Falcon Merger Sub 1, Inc., Falcon Merger Sub 2, LLC and Roku, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“ Roku ”), are parties to that certain Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated as of June 14, 2026 (the “ Merger Agreement ”), pursuant to which, among other things and on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth therein, the Company will acquire Roku. Capitalized terms used in these recitals and not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed thereto in the Merger Agreement; WHEREAS , Roku sponsors the Roku, Inc. Amended and Restated 2017 Equity Incentive Plan (the “ Roku Plan ”), which is a pre-existing equity compensation plan that was approved by Roku’s stockholders prior to, and not adopted in contemplation of, the Merger; WHEREAS , Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c) and IM-5635-1 permit shares that remain available for future issuance under a pre-existing, stockholder-approved plan of an acquired company to be used for post-closing awards under the acquiror’s equity compensation plan without approval of the acquiror’s stockholders, provided that such shares (1) are appropriately adjusted to reflect the transaction, (2) are not used beyond the period during which they would have been available for issuance under the pre-existing plan, absent the transaction, and (3) are not used for awards to individuals who were employed by the acquiror or its subsidiaries (other than Roku and its subsidiaries) as of the Effective Time; WHEREAS , the Company desires to amend the Plan, effective as of the Effective Time and subject to and contingent upon the occurrence of the Closing, to provide that the shares that remain available for future issuance under the Roku Plan as of immediately prior to the Effective Time, as converted into shares of Common Stock based on the Adjustment Ratio, may be used for awards under the Plan as a separate, additive share reserve, subject to the limitations set forth in this Amendment; and WHEREAS , pursuant to Article VIII of the Plan, the Board has the authority to alter, amend, suspend or terminate the Plan at any time, in whole or in part, without stockholder approval except where stockholder approval is required by law or under the rules of the Nasdaq Global Select Market or other principal stock exchange on which the Common Stock is then listed. NOW, THEREFORE , the Plan is hereby amended as follows: ARTICLE I AMENDMENT Section 1. New Definitions. Section 1.2 of the Plan is hereby amended to add the following new defined terms, to be inserted in appropriate alphabetical order: “ Adjustment Ratio ” shall mean the sum of (a) the Exchange Ratio plus (b) the quotient obtained by dividing the Per Share Cash Amount by the Parent Measurement Price. “ Effective Time ” shall have the meaning set forth in the Merger Agreement. “ Exchange Ratio ” shall have the meaning set forth in the Merger Agreement. “ Grant Period End Date ” shall mean January 1, 2034, which is the date on which the automatic annual increase to the share reserve under Section 3(a) of the Roku Plan was, by its terms, scheduled to cease, and which the Company has determined is the appropriate outside date through which shares would have remained available for grant under the Roku Plan absent the consummation of the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement. “ Legacy Fox Service Provider ” shall mean any individual who was an employee of the Company or any of its Affiliates (excluding, for this purpose, Roku, Inc. and its subsidiaries) as of the Effective Time. “ Merger Agreement ” shall mean the Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated as of June 14, 2026, by and among the Company, Falcon Merger Sub 1, Inc., Falcon Merger Sub 2, LLC and Roku, Inc., as it may be amended from time to time. “ Parent Measurement Price ” shall have the meaning set forth in the Merger Agreement. “ Per Share Cash Amount ” shall have the meaning set forth in the Merger Agreement. “ Roku Assumed Share Reserve ” shall have the meaning set forth in Section 1.5(c) of the Plan. “ Roku Plan ” shall mean the Roku, Inc. Amended and Restated 2017 Equity Incentive Plan, as in effect immediately prior to the Effective Time. “ Substitute Roku Award ” shall mean an Award granted, or shares of Common Stock issued, by the Company in assumption of, or in substitution or exchange for, a Roku equity award outstanding as of immediately prior to the Effective Time, as provided for in Section 2.02 of the Merger Agreement. Section 2 . Roku Assumed Share Reserve. Section 1.5 of the Plan is hereby amended to add the following new subsection (c): “(c) Roku Assumed Share Reserve. Without limiting the generality of Section 1.5(a) , in connection with the Merger Agreement, as of the Effective Time, an additional 91,944,833 shares of Common Stock (the “ Roku Assumed Share Reserve ”), representing the number of shares of common stock of Roku, Inc. that remained available for future issuance under the Roku Plan as of immediately prior to the Effective Time, converted into shares of Common Stock based on the Adjustment Ratio and rounded down to the nearest whole share, shall be available for the grant of Awards under the Plan, subject to the terms of this Section 1.5(c) . The Roku Assumed Share Reserve shall be in addition to, and shall not reduce or be drawn from, the shares of Common Stock authorized for issuance under Section 1.5(a) , and the Roku Assumed Share Reserve shall not count against, and shall not be counted as part of, the Section 1.5 Limit. Notwithstanding the foregoing or anything else in the Plan to the contrary, Awards from the Roku Assumed Share Reserve may be granted only in accordance with the following conditions: (i) Exchange Compliance : Awards from the Roku Assumed Share Reserve shall be made only to the extent such Awards are permitted to be made without approval of the Company’s stockholders under the rules of the Nasdaq Global Select Market (or such other principal stock exchange on which the Common Stock is then listed), including Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c) and IM-5635-1 or any successor rule; (ii) Eligible Recipients : Awards from the Roku Assumed Share Reserve shall not be granted to any Legacy Fox Service Provider. For the avoidance of doubt, Awards from the Roku Assumed Share Reserve may be granted to any employee, director or other Service Provider of the Company or any of its Affiliates (including Roku, Inc. and its subsidiaries following the Effective Time) who is not a Legacy Fox Service Provider, whether such person’s Service with the Company or its Affiliates commenced before, upon or after the Effective Time; (iii) Grant Period : No Award using shares from the Roku Assumed Share Reserve shall be granted on or after the Grant Period End Date; (iv) Capitalization Adjustments : The number of shares constituting the Roku Assumed Share Reserve, and the number of shares subject to any outstanding Award granted from the Roku Assumed Share Reserve, shall be subject to adjustment in accordance with Article VI of the Plan to the same extent as shares subject to the Section 1.5 Limit; and (v) No Incentive Stock Options : No Award granted from the Roku Assumed Share Reserve shall be an Incentive Stock Option. To the extent permitted by law or the rules of the Nasdaq Global Select Market (or such other principal stock exchange on which the Common Stock is then listed), shares subject to an Award granted from the Roku Assumed Share Reserve that for any reason expires, is cancelled, forfeited or terminated without having been exercised or paid, or that is instead settled in cash, shall be added back to, and shall again become available for Awards under, the Roku Assumed Share Reserve (and not the Section 1.5 Limit), subject to the same share-counting principles set forth in Section 1.5(b) of the Plan and to the conditions of this Section 1.5(c) . Any shares of Common Stock underlying Substitute Roku Awards granted pursuant to the Merger Agreement shall not be counted against, and shall not reduce, the Roku Assumed Share Reserve or the Section 1.5 Limit, consistent with Section 1.5(b)(iii) of the Plan, except that shares of Common Stock acquired upon exercise of a Substitute Roku Award that is an Incentive Stock Option shall count against the maximum number of shares of Common Stock that may be issued pursuant to Incentive Stock Options under Section 1.5(a) of the Plan.” Section 3. Effectiveness. This Amendment shall become effective as of, and is expressly subject to and contingent upon the occurrence of, the Effective Time. If the Merger Agreement is terminated for any reason prior to the Closing, this Amendment shall be void ab initio and of no further force or effect, and the Plan shall continue in effect without giving effect to this Amendment. Section 4. No Other Amendment. Except as expressly amended hereby, the Plan shall remain in full force and effect in accordance with its terms. Remainder of Page Intentionally Left Blank

text: EX-10.1 3 ea031100201ex10-1.htm PURCHASE AGREEMENT DATED NOVEMBER 4, 2026, BY AND BETWEEN THE COMPANY AND JIAWEI WANG Exhibit 10.1 Purchase Agreement This Purchase Agreement (this “ Agreement ”) is made as of November 4, 2026, by and between the purchaser listed on the signature page hereto (the “ Purchaser ”) and Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. , a Delaware corporation (the “ Company ”). Recitals Whereas , the Company desires to sell to the Purchaser, and the Purchaser desires to purchase from the Company, one (1) share of Series A Preferred Stock, par value $0.0001 per share (“ Series A Preferred Stock ”), for the purchase price of $100.00 (the “ Purchase Price ”); and Whereas , the Series A Preferred Stock shall have the rights, preferences, privileges, qualifications, limitations and restrictions set forth in the Certificate of Designation of Series A Preferred Stock (the “ Series A COD ”), substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A , which shall be filed by the Company with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware prior to the Closing (as defined below). Now, Therefore , in consideration of the foregoing premises and the respective representations and warranties, covenants and agreements contained herein, the receipt and sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, the Company and the Purchaser agree as follows: Article I: Sale and Purchase 1.1. Upon the terms and subject to the conditions herein contained, the Company agrees to sell to the Purchaser, and the Purchaser agrees to purchase from the Company, at the Closing, one (1) share of Series A Preferred Stock for the Purchase Price. The sale and purchase of the share of Series A Preferred Stock pursuant to this Agreement is referred to herein as the “ Stock Purchase .” 1.2. At or prior to the Closing, the Purchaser will pay the Purchase Price by wire transfer of immediately available funds in accordance with wire instructions provided by the Company to the Purchaser prior to the Closing, or by check or money order payable to the Company. 1.3. Subject to the satisfaction of each of the conditions set forth in Article IV and Article V hereof (to the extent not waived in accordance therewith), the closing of the Stock Purchase (the “ Closing ”) shall take place remotely on the date hereof via the exchange of documents and signatures (the date on which such Closing occurs is hereinafter referred to as the “ Closing Date ”). Article II: Covenants, Representations and Warranties of the Purchaser The Purchaser hereby covenants as follows, and makes the following representations and warranties, each of which is and shall be true and correct on the date hereof, to the Company. All such covenants, representations and warranties shall survive the Closing. 2.1. Power and Authorization. The Purchaser has the power, authority and capacity to execute and deliver this Agreement, to perform his obligations hereunder, and to consummate the Stock Purchase contemplated hereby. 2.2. Valid and Enforceable Agreement; No Violations. This Agreement has been duly executed and delivered by the Purchaser and constitutes a legal, valid and binding obligation of the Purchaser, enforceable against the Purchaser in accordance with its terms, except that such enforcement may be subject to (a) bankruptcy, insolvency, fraudulent transfer, reorganization, moratorium or other similar laws affecting or relating to enforcement of creditors’ rights generally, and (b) general principles of equity, whether such enforceability is considered in a proceeding at law or in equity (the “ Enforceability Exceptions ”). This Agreement and the consummation of the Stock Purchase will not materially violate, conflict with or result in a breach of or default under (i) any agreement or instrument to which the Purchaser is a party or by which the Purchaser or any of his assets are bound, or (ii) any laws, regulations or governmental or judicial decrees, injunctions or orders applicable to the Purchaser. 2.3. Accredited Investor. The Purchaser is an “accredited investor” within the meaning of Rule 501(a) of Regulation D promulgated under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “ Securities Act ”), and is acquiring the Series A Preferred Stock hereunder for investment for his own account and not with a view to, or for resale in connection with, any distribution thereof in a manner that would violate the registration requirements of the Securities Act. Purchaser is able (i) to bear the economic risk of its investment in the Company, (ii) to hold the Series A Preferred Stock for an indefinite period of time, and (iii) presently and, based on existing conditions, hereafter to afford a complete loss of such investments. In making its decision to invest in the Company, Purchaser has relied solely upon independent investigations made by it and by its own professional financial and other advisors. Purchaser has been given the opportunity to obtain information and to examine all documents relating to the Company, and to ask questions of, and to receive answers from, the Company or any persons acting on their behalf concerning the Company and the terms and conditions of this investment, and to obtain any additional information it desires to verify the accuracy of any information previously furnished. All such questions have been answered to Purchaser’s full satisfaction, and all information and documents, records and books pertaining to this investment which it has requested have been made available to it. 2.4. No Public Market. The Purchaser acknowledges and agrees that no public market exists (and it is likely that none will ever exist) for the Series A Preferred Stock and the share of Series A Preferred Stock is subject to transfer restrictions as set forth in the Series A COD. 2.5. Transfer Restrictions. The Purchaser acknowledges and agrees as follows: (a) The Series A Preferred Stock has not been registered for sale under the Securities Act, in reliance on Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act; the Company does not currently intend to register the Series A Preferred Stock under the Securities Act at any time in the future. (b) The Purchaser understands that there are substantial restrictions on the transferability of the Series A Preferred Stock and that the book-entry certificate representing the Series A Preferred Stock will bear restrictive legends in substantially the following form (and a stop-transfer order may be placed against transfer of such certificates or other instruments): THE SECURITIES REPRESENTED HEREBY HAVE NOT BEEN REGISTERED UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OF 1933, AS AMENDED (THE “SECURITIES ACT”), OR ANY STATE SECURITIES LAWS, AND NEITHER SUCH SECURITIES NOR ANY INTEREST THEREIN MAY BE OFFERED, SOLD, PLEDGED, ASSIGNED OR OTHERWISE TRANSFERRED UNLESS (1) A REGISTRATION STATEMENT WITH RESPECT THERETO IS EFFECTIVE UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT AND ANY APPLICABLE STATE SECURITIES LAWS, OR (2) AN EXEMPTION FROM SUCH REGISTRATION EXISTS AND THE COMPANY RECEIVES AN OPINION OF COUNSEL REASONABLY SATISFACTORY TO THE COMPANY, THAT SUCH SECURITIES MAY BE OFFERED, SOLD, PLEDGED, ASSIGNED OR TRANSFERRED IN THE MANNER CONTEMPLATED WITHOUT AN EFFECTIVE REGISTRATION STATEMENT UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OR APPLICABLE STATE SECURITIES LAWS. THE SECURITIES REPRESENTED HEREBY ARE ALSO SUBJECT TO TRANSFER RESTRICTIONS AS SET FORTH IN THE CERTIFICATE OF DESIGNATION OF PREFERENCES, RIGHTS AND LIMITATIONS OF SERIES A PREFERRED STOCK. OTHER THAN FOR A REDEMPTION PURSUANT TO AND IN ACCORDANCE WITH SECTION 6, THE SECURITIES REPRESENTED BY THIS CERTIFICATE MAY NOT BE TRANSFERRED AT ANY TIME WITHOUT THE PRIOR WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE CORPORATION. Article III: Covenants, Representations and Warranties of the Company The Company hereby covenants as follows, and makes the following representations and warranties, each of which is and shall be true and correct on the date hereof, to the Purchaser. All such covenants, representations and warranties shall survive the Closing. 3.1. Power and Authorization. The Company is duly incorporated, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of its state of incorporation, and has the power, authority and capacity to execute and deliver this Agreement, to perform its obligations hereunder, and to consummate the Stock Purchase contemplated hereby. 2 3.2. Valid and Enforceable Agreement; No Violations. This Agreement has been duly executed and delivered by the Company and constitutes a legal, valid and binding obligation of the Company, enforceable against it in accordance with its terms, except that such enforcement may be subject to the Enforceability Exceptions. The issuance of the Series A Preferred Stock has been duly authorized by the Company. This Agreement, the issuance of the Series A Preferred Stock and consummation of the Stock Purchase will not violate, conflict with or result in a breach of or default under (a) the charter, bylaws or other organizational documents of the Company, (b) any agreement or instrument to which the Company is a party or by which the Company or any of its assets are bound, or (c) any laws, regulations or governmental or judicial decrees, injunctions or orders applicable to the Company. 3.3. Securities Law Matters. Assuming the accuracy of the Purchaser’s representations and warranties hereunder, the Series A Preferred Stock issued pursuant to the Stock Purchase will be (a) exempt from the registration requirements of the Securities Act pursuant to Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act, and (b) issued in compliance with all applicable state and federal laws concerning the issuance of the Series A Preferred Stock. 3.4. Validity of the Series A Preferred Stock. The share of Series A Preferred Stock to be issued pursuant to this Agreement at the Closing (a) has been duly authorized by the Company and, upon its issuance pursuant to the Stock Purchase in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, the Series A Preferred Stock will be validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable and (b) will not, as of the date of issuance, be subject to any preemptive, participation, rights of first refusal or other similar rights. Article IV: Conditions to Company’s Obligations at Closing The Company’s obligation to complete the Stock Purchase and deliver the Series A Preferred Stock to the Purchaser in exchange for the Purchase Price shall be subject to the following conditions to the extent not waived by the Company: 4.1. Representation and Warranties. The representations and warranties made by the Purchaser in Article II hereof shall be true and correct in all material respects (except to the extent any such representation and warranty is qualified by materiality, in which case, such representation and warranty shall be true and correct in all respects as so qualified) as of the Closing Date, except to the extent any such representation or warranty expressly speaks as of an earlier date, in which case such representation or warranty shall be true and correct as of such earlier date. 4.2. Performance. The Purchaser shall have performed in all material respects all obligations and covenants herein required to be performed by it at or prior to the Closing. Article V: Conditions to Purchaser’s Obligations at Closing The Purchaser’s obligation to deliver the Purchase Price and accept delivery of the Series A Preferred Stock and to effect the Stock Purchase shall be subject to the following conditions to the extent not waived by the Purchaser: 5.1. Representations and Warranties. The representations and warranties made by the Company in Article III hereof shall be true and correct in all material respects (except to the extent any such representation and warranty is qualified by materiality, in which case, such representation and warranty shall be true and correct in all respects as so qualified) as of the Closing Date, except to the extent any such representation or warranty expressly speaks as of an earlier date, in which case such representation or warranty shall be true and correct as of such earlier date. 5.2. Performance. The Company shall have performed in all material respects all obligations and covenants herein required to be performed by it at or prior to the Closing. 5.3. Judgments. No judgment, writ, order, injunction, award or decree of or by any court, or judge, justice or magistrate, including any bankruptcy court or judge, or any order of or by any governmental authority, shall have been issued, and no action or proceeding shall have been instituted by any governmental authority, enjoining or preventing the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby. 3 5.4. Certificate of Designation. The Company shall have filed the Series A COD with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, and the Series A COD shall remain in full force and effect as of the Closing. Article VI: Voting Agreement 6.1. Voting Agreement. Purchaser hereby covenants and agrees to vote the share of Series A Preferred Stock (which shall have 500,000,000 votes) on the Shareholder Proposal (as defined in the Series A COD) for or against such proposal in the same proportion as shares of the Company’s common stock, par value $0.0001 per share (the “ Common Stock ”), are voted (excluding any shares of Common Stock that are not voted, whether due to abstentions, broker non-votes or otherwise) on such proposal; provided , however , that unless and until at least one-third of the outstanding shares of Common Stock on the record date set for the meeting of stockholders at which the Shareholder Proposal is presented are present in person, by remote communication, if applicable, or by proxy at such meeting, the Purchaser will not vote the share of Series A Preferred Stock on such Shareholder Proposal. Article VII: Miscellaneous 7.1. Entire Agreement. This Agreement, and any other documents and agreements executed in connection with this Agreement or the Stock Purchase, including the Series A COD, constitute the entire agreement and understanding of the parties hereto pertaining to the subject matter hereof and supersede all prior and contemporaneous oral or written agreements, representations, warranties, contracts, correspondence, conversations, memoranda and understandings between or among the parties or any of their agents, representatives or affiliates relative to such subject matter, including, without limitation, any emails or draft documents. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall be enforceable by and inure solely to the benefit of, the Company and the Purchaser and their respective successors and permitted assigns; provided, however, that neither this Agreement nor any of the rights hereunder may be assigned without the prior written consent of the other party to this Agreement, and any attempted assignment of this Agreement or any of such rights without such consent shall be void and of no effect. 7.2. Amendment. This Agreement may not be amended except by an instrument in writing signed on behalf of each of the parties to this Agreement. 7.3. Construction. References in the singular shall include the plural, and vice versa, unless the context otherwise requires. References in the masculine shall include the feminine and neuter, and vice versa, unless the context otherwise requires. Headings in this Agreement are for convenience of reference only and shall not limit or otherwise affect the meanings of the provisions hereof. No party, nor its respective counsel, shall be deemed the drafter of this Agreement for purposes of construing the provisions of this Agreement, and all language in all parts of this Agreement shall be construed in accordance with its fair meaning, and not strictly for or against any party. 7.4. Costs and Expenses. The Company shall pay all costs and expenses incurred by it and the Purchaser in connection with the negotiation, preparation, execution and performance of this Agreement, including, but not limited to, attorneys’ fees. 7.5. Notices. All notices and other communications given or made pursuant to this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed effectively given upon the earlier of actual receipt, or (a) personal delivery to the party to be notified, (b) when sent, if sent by electronic mail or facsimile during normal business hours of the recipient, and if not sent during normal business hours, then on the recipient’s next business day, (c) five days after having been sent by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, or (d) one business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier, freight prepaid, specifying next business day delivery, with written verification of receipt. All communications shall be sent to the respective parties at their address as set forth on the signature page, or to such e-mail address, facsimile number or address as subsequently modified by written notice given in accordance with this Section 7.5 . 4 7.6. Governing Law. This Agreement shall in all respects be construed in accordance with and governed by the substantive laws of the State of Delaware, without reference to its choice of law rules to the extent they would direct any matter hereunder to (or apply the laws of) any other jurisdiction. 7.7. Severability. If one or more provisions of this Agreement are held to be unenforceable under applicable law, the parties agree to renegotiate such provision in good faith. In the event that the parties cannot reach a mutually agreeable and enforceable replacement for such provision, then (a) such provision shall be excluded from this Agreement, (b) the balance of the Agreement shall be interpreted as if such provision were so excluded and (c) the balance of the Agreement shall be enforceable in accordance with its terms. 7.8. Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, but all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Counterparts may be delivered via facsimile, electronic mail (including pdf or any electronic signature complying with the U.S. federal ESIGN Act of 2000, the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act or other applicable law, e.g. , www.docusign.com) or other transmission method and any counterpart so delivered shall be deemed to have been duly and validly delivered and be valid and effective for all purposes. title: NEXTNRG, INC.
text: EX-10.1 3 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 DEBT EXCHANGE AGREEMENT This DEBT EXCHANGE AGREEMENT (this “ Agreement ”) is dated as of November 2, 2026 (the “ Effective Date ”) and is entered into by and among NextNRG, Inc. , a Nevada corporation (“ NextNRG ”), NextNRG Holding Corp., a Nevada corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of NextNRG (“ NXXT Sub ” and, together with NextNRG, the “ Company ”), and Michael D. Farkas (the “ Holder ”). RECITALS A. The Holder holds the promissory notes issued by NextNRG or NXXT Subas set forth on Schedule 1 (the “ Exchanged Notes ”), with an aggregate outstanding principal amount of $3,629,924 and accrued and unpaid interest of $2,749,169, and NXXT Sub owes the Holder accrued and unpaid fees of $620,907 for the Holder’s personal guarantees of the Company’s obligations described on Schedule 1 (the “ Guarantee Fees ”), in each case as of the Effective Date (together, $7,000,000, the “ Exchanged Amount ”). B. Michael D. Farkas is the Chief Executive Officer, a director and a principal stockholder of NextNRG. The transactions contemplated by this Agreement are therefore related-party transactions subject to NRS 78.140 and Nasdaq Rule 5630. C. The Board of Directors of NextNRG (the “ Board ”), acting on the recommendation of the audit committee of the Board (the “ Audit Committee ”), has authorized the designation of 7,000 shares of a new series of preferred stock of NextNRG to be known as the Series D Convertible Voting Preferred Stock, par value $0.0001 per share (the “ Series D Preferred ”), pursuant to the Certificate of Designations of Preferences and Rights of Series D Convertible Voting Preferred Stock, substantially in the form attached as Exhibit C (the “ Certificate of Designations ”). D. The parties wish to satisfy and discharge the Company’s obligations with respect to the Exchanged Notes and the Guarantee Fees in exchange for the issuance to the Holder of shares of Series D Preferred on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement and the Certificate of Designations. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants in this Agreement, the parties agree as follows: 1. DEFINITIONS Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Agreement shall have the meanings given to them in the Certificate of Designations. In addition: (a) “ Affiliate ” has the meaning given to “affiliate” in Rule 144 under the Securities Act. (b) “ Conversion Price ” means $2.20 per share, being not less than the greater of (i) the consolidated closing bid price of the Common Stock on the Trading Market and (ii) the “Minimum Price” as defined in Nasdaq Rule 5635(d)(1)(A), in each case measured immediately prior to the date of this Agreement, as adjusted under the Certificate of Designations and Section 3.5 below. 1 (c) “ Securities Act ” means the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. (d) “ Series C Consent ” means the Limited Consent and Waiver, dated as of November 2, 2026, by and among NextNRG and the holders of the shares of Series C Preferred, as acknowledged by the Holder. 2. THE EXCHANGE 2.1 Exchange. At the Closing (as defined below), the Holder will surrender to the Company all of its right, title and interest in, to and under the Exchanged Notes and the Guarantee Fees and, in exchange, NextNRG will issue to the Holder 7,000 shares of Series D Preferred (the “ Exchange Shares ”), being the Exchanged Amount divided by the initial Stated Value of $1,000 per share. The Exchange Shares are the sole consideration for the Exchanged Notes and the Guarantee Fees, and no cash or other property will be paid in respect of them. 2.2 Satisfaction and Release. Upon the issuance of the Exchange Shares, (i) the Exchanged Notes, and all principal, interest, fees and other obligations under them, and (ii) the Guarantee Fees, will be surrendered and cancelled in full, and any security interest, guaranty or other credit support for any of such Exchanged Notes or Guarantee Fees will be released. The Holder will return the original Exchanged Notes (or deliver a customary lost-note affidavit) and will sign any lien releases the Company reasonably requests. 2.3 Excluded Obligations. Nothing in this Agreement satisfies, cancels, waives or releases any indebtedness, fees, compensation or other amounts owed by the Company or any of its subsidiaries to the Holder or any of its Affiliates that are not listed on Schedule 1 (the “ Excluded Obligations ”), each of which is listed on Schedule 2. The Excluded Obligations remain outstanding, subject to this Section 2.3. For so long as any Series C Preferred is outstanding, no Excluded Obligation will be paid, prepaid or satisfied in cash or other property except as permitted by Section 5(d) of the Voting Agreement and the Series C Certificate of Designation. 2.4 Closing. The closing (the “ Closing ”) will take place electronically on the first Business Day on which all of the conditions in Section 2.5 have been satisfied or, to the extent permitted, waived, or on such other date as NextNRG, NXXT Sub and the Holder agree in writing (the “ Closing Date ”); provided that the condition set forth in Section 2.5(b) may not be waived. 2.5 Conditions to Closing. The obligations of each party to effect the Closing are subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the following conditions: (a) the Audit Committee and the Board have approved this Agreement and the Certificate of Designations, and the Certificate of Designations has been filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Nevada; (b) NextNRG shall have received a copy of the duly executed Series C Consent and NextNRG shall have received each other consent required under any agreement to which it or any of its subsidiaries is a party; (c) NextNRG shall have filed a Notification Form: Listing of Additional Shares with Nasdaq for all the Conversion Shares (disclosing the Notice Cap under Section 6(g) of the Certificate of Designations) and confirmed that no shareholder approval is required under Nasdaq rules for the issuance of the Series D Preferred; 2 (d) the representations and warranties of each party shall be true and correct at the Closing, and each party shall have performed each of its obligations required to be performed at or before the Closing; (e) NextNRG shall have delivered to such Holder evidence of the filing and acceptance of the Certificate of Designations from the Secretary of State of the State of Nevada; (f) the Holder shall have delivered to the Company the Exchanged Notes and the releases under Section 2.2 herein; and (g) the NextNRG shall have delivered to the Holder the Exchange Shares in DRS book-entry form. 2.6 Termination. Any party may terminate this Agreement by written notice to the other if the Closing has not occurred by, November 6, 2026; provided that this right is not available to a party whose breach caused the Closing not to occur by that date. 3. SERIES D PREFERRED; HOLDER COVENANTS 3.1 Certificate of Designations Governs. The powers, preferences, rights, qualifications, limitations and restrictions of the Series D Preferred (including as to dividends, ranking, liquidation, conversion, adjustments to the Conversion Price, the Notice Cap, voting, transfer and Reconversion) are set forth exclusively in the Certificate of Designations, and nothing in this Agreement grants any holder of Series D Preferred any right in respect of the Series D Preferred that is not set forth in the Certificate of Designations. The covenants of the Holder and the Company in this Agreement are in addition to, and are not limited by, the Certificate of Designations. 3.2 Voting Covenants. (a) The Holder shall not, and shall cause each of its Affiliates not to, exercise its voting rights, as a stockholder or otherwise, for the purpose of causing, requiring or preventing a Reconversion, or of changing the composition or authority of the Audit Committee in relation to a Reconversion. (b) For so long as any Series C Preferred is outstanding, the Holder shall, and shall cause of its Affiliates to, vote (or act by written consent with respect to) all shares of shares of capital stock of the NextNRG held by it or any of its Affiliates (i) in favor of any increase in the authorized shares of Common Stock, and any other stockholder approval, required under the Series C Certificate of Designation or the Securities Purchase Agreement, and (ii) in favor of any amendment of the Series C Certificate of Designation approved by the Series C Required Holders, and will not vote against, or take any action to impede, any of the foregoing. 3.3 Resale Limitation. For so long as any shares of Series C Preferred are outstanding, the Holder shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, (a) sell or otherwise dispose of, on any trading day, Conversion Shares in excess of 5% of the aggregate daily trading volume of the Common Stock on the Trading Market for that trading day, or (b) engage in any short sale of, or any hedging or derivative transaction with respect to, the Common Stock. 3 3.4 Transfers. The Holder will not sell, assign, pledge or otherwise transfer any shares of Series D Preferred or any Reinstated Note, or any Conversion Shares other than in a sale that complies with Section 3.3, unless the transferee first agrees in writing, for the benefit of NextNRG and the holders of the Series C Preferred, to be bound by Section 2.3, this Section 3 and Section 4. 4. RECONVERSION 4.1 Certificate of Designations Governs. NextNRG may effect a Reconversion only in accordance with Section 7 of the Certificate of Designations (including Section 7(g)) and this Section 4. NextNRG will deliver a copy of each Reconversion Notice to each holder of Series C Preferred concurrently with its delivery to the Holder. 4.2 Solvency Determination. Before delivering any Reconversion Notice, the Audit Committee will determine, and NextNRG will certify in writing to the Holder and the Series C Required Holders, that after giving effect to the Reconversion NextNRG would be able to pay its debts as they become due in the usual course of business and that its total assets would not be less than the sum of its total liabilities plus the amount that would be needed, if NextNRG were dissolved at that time, to satisfy the preferential rights of the holders of the Series C Preferred and any other stockholders senior to the Series D Preferred. 4.3 Reinstated Note. Each Reinstated Note will be substantially on the terms set forth in Exhibit A, will comply with Section 7(g) of the Certificate of Designations (which controls in the event of any conflict with Exhibit A) and will be in the form agreed by NextNRG and the Holder before the Closing, which form must be reasonably satisfactory to the Series C Required Holders. No Reinstated Note may be amended or modified except in compliance with this Section 4.3 and Section 7.8. 4.4 Holder Acknowledgements. The Holder agrees that: (a) the Reinstated Note will be unsecured and will be subject to a subordination agreement in form and substance satisfactory to the Series C Required Holders and any intercreditor agreement required by NextNRG’s senior lenders at the time, and will constitute Stockholder Debt (as defined in the Voting Agreement) subject to Section 5(d) of the Voting Agreement; (b) the Reinstated Note will not have the benefit of any security interest, guaranty or other credit support that secured or supported the Exchanged Notes; and (c) it will sign any subordination agreement or other document NextNRG reasonably requests to give effect to a Reconversion. 4.5 Accounting Intent. The parties intend that the Series D Preferred be classified as permanent stockholders’ equity. The Reconversion right is an option solely of NextNRG, exercisable only by directors independent of the Holder, and does not give the Holder any right to cash or other assets. The conversion right is settled only in shares of Common Stock at a fixed price. If NextNRG’s independent auditor advises that any provision prevents that classification, the parties will negotiate in good faith to amend this Agreement and the Certificate of Designations to the minimum extent needed, subject in each case to Section 4A(d) of the Certificate of Designations and Section 7.8. 4 5. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF THE COMPANY NextNRG, on behalf of itself and Next Sub, hereby represents and warrants to the Holder that, as of the date hereof and as of the Closing: (a) NextNRG is duly organized and in good standing under Nevada law, and has the corporate power to enter into and perform this Agreement; (b) this Agreement has been duly authorized by the Audit Committee and the Board and the board of directors of Next Sub and is a valid and binding obligation of the Company, enforceable against the Company in accordance with its terms, subject to bankruptcy, insolvency and similar laws affecting creditors’ rights generally and to general principles of equity; (c) when issued by NextNRG under this Agreement, the Exchange Shares will be, and when issued by NextNRG on conversion the Conversion Shares will be, duly authorized, validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable, free of liens created by NextNRG; (d) the Conversion Price is not less than the greater of the consolidated closing bid price of the Common Stock and the Minimum Price (as defined in Nasdaq Rule 5635(d)(1)(A)), each measured immediately prior to the date of this Agreement and no shareholder approval is required for the issuance of the Exchange Shares under applicable Nasdaq rules; (e) the amounts of principal, accrued interest and Guarantee Fees set forth on Schedule 1 are true, correct and complete, and together equal the Exchanged Amount; and if any such amount is understated, the shortfall will be an Excluded Obligation subject to Section 2.3 and will constitute Stockholder Debt (as defined in the Voting Agreement); (f) the Series C Consent has been duly executed by all parties thereto and each condition set forth in paragraph 7 of the Series C Consent that is required to be satisfied at or before the Effective Date and Closing Date has been satisfied; (g) subject to receipt of the consents described in Section 2.5(b), the execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by the Company do not breach the articles of incorporation or bylaws of NextNRG or any of its subsidiaries, or any material agreement or law binding on any of them; and (h) it has not, nor has any Person acting on its behalf, directly or indirectly made any offers or sales of any security or solicited any offers to buy any security under circumstances that would cause the transactions contemplated by this Agreement and the issuance of the Exchanged Shares pursuant to this Agreement to be integrated with prior offerings by NextNRG for purposes of the Securities Act which would prevent the Company from delivering the Exchanged Shares to the Holders pursuant to Section 3(a)(9) of the Securities Act or Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act, nor will the Company take any action or steps that would cause the transactions contemplated by this Agreement to be integrated with other offerings to the effect that the delivery of the Exchanged Shares to the Holders would be seen not to be exempt pursuant to Section 3(a)(9) of the Securities Act or Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act. As used in this Agreement, “ Person ” means an individual or corporation, partnership, trust, incorporated or unincorporated association, joint venture, limited liability company, joint stock company, government (or an agency or subdivision thereof) or other entity of any kind. 5 6. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF THE HOLDER The Holder hereby represents and warrants to the Company that, as of the date hereof and as of the Closing: (a) it is the sole legal and beneficial owner of the Exchanged Notes and of the right to receive the Guarantee Fees, free of any lien, participation or other interest, and has not assigned any part of them; (b) the amounts of principal, accrued interest and Guarantee Fees set forth on Schedule 1 are correct and together equal the Exchanged Amount, and, other than the Exchanged Amount and the Excluded Obligations listed on Schedule 2, no amount is owed by the Company or any of its subsidiaries to the Holder or any of its Affiliates; (c) it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement, which is its valid and binding obligation; (d) it is an “accredited investor” under Rule 501(a) of Regulation D, is acquiring the Exchange Shares (and any Conversion Shares) for its own account and not with a view to distribution, and understands they are “restricted securities” that have not been registered under the Securities Act; (e) it has had access to all information about the Company it considers necessary, including NextNRG’s Nasdaq listing status, stockholders’ deficit and going-concern disclosure, and the terms of the Series C Preferred and the Series C Transaction Documents; and (f) it has consulted its own legal and tax advisers and is not relying on the Company for tax advice, including on the tax effect of the exchange, any PIK accretion or any Reconversion. 7. COVENANTS 7.1 Related-Party Approvals. NextNRG has obtained, and will maintain records of, the approval of this Agreement by the Audit Committee and the Board under NRS 78.140 and Nasdaq Rule 5630. NXXT Sub has obtained, and will maintain records of, the approval of this Agreement by its board of directors and any other necessary parties. 7.2 Series C Consent. NextNRG will comply, and will cause its subsidiaries to comply, with each condition and covenant set forth in the Series C Consent, and the Holder will comply with each condition and covenant set forth in the Series C Consent that applies to it. 7.3 Nasdaq Notification. On or before the Closing Date, NextNRG will file a Notification Form: Listing of Additional Shares with Nasdaq for all the Conversion Shares, disclosing the Notice Cap and the Cap Release Date (as provided in Section 6(g) of the Certificate of Designations), and will respond promptly to any Nasdaq inquiry. NextNRG will notify the Holder in writing of the Cap Release Date. 6 7.4 Disclosure. NextNRG will file a Current Report on Form 8-K describing this Agreement within the time required by Form 8-K or such earlier date as required by the Series C Consent. The Holder will make each filing required of it under Section 13(d) or Section 16 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (including a Form 4 and an amendment to its Schedule 13D). 7.5 [ Reserved ]. 7.6 Exemption. The parties intend the exchange to be exempt from registration under Section 3(a)(9) of the Securities Act or, alternatively, Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act. 7.7 Legends. The Exchange Shares will bear the legend set forth in Section 11(a) of the Certificate of Designations, and any Reinstated Note and, until eligible for removal under Section 6(c) of the Certificate of Designations, any Conversion Shares will bear customary restrictive legends. 7.8 Series C Third-Party Beneficiaries. The holders of the Series C Preferred are express third-party beneficiaries of Sections 2.3, 2.4, 2.5(b), 3, 4, 5(e), 6(b), 7.2, 7.8, 8.2, 8.3 and 8.6 and may enforce them directly. For so long as any Series C Preferred is outstanding, (a) no provision of this Agreement may be amended or waived, and this Agreement may not be terminated, in any manner that is adverse to the holders of the Series C Preferred without the prior written consent of the Series C Required Holders, and (b) no Reinstated Note may be issued other than in compliance with Section 4.3 and Section 7(g) of the Certificate of Designations. 8. MISCELLANEOUS 8.1 Governing Law; Forum. This Agreement is governed by Nevada law. Each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state courts located in Miami-Dade County, Florida (or, if they lack jurisdiction, the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida, Miami Division). Nothing in this Section 8.1 limits the right of any holder of Series C Preferred to enforce this Agreement in any forum permitted under the Series C Transaction Documents. 8.2 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, the Certificate of Designations and any Reinstated Note constitute the entire agreement among the parties with respect to their subject matter and supersede all prior understandings among them with respect thereto; provided that nothing in this Agreement supersedes, limits or otherwise modifies the Series C Consent (including the Holder’s acknowledgment of it), the Voting Agreement (including any amendment to it) or any other Series C Transaction Document. 8.3 Amendment and Waiver. This Agreement may be amended or waived only by a written instrument signed by NextNRG and the Holder. Any amendment or waiver by the Company requires the approval of the Audit Committee. Any amendment or waiver is also subject to Section 7.8. 8.4 Assignment. The Holder may not assign this Agreement except to a transferee of Series D Preferred in a transfer that complies with Section 3.4 and Section 10 of the Certificate of Designations. The Company may assign it to a successor by merger or similar transaction. 8.5 Further Assurances. Each party will sign and deliver any further documents reasonably needed to carry out this Agreement, including at a Reconversion. 8.6 Severability. If any provision is held invalid, the rest of this Agreement remains in effect, and the invalid provision will be reformed to the minimum extent needed, consistent with Section 4.5; provided that no such reformation will limit Section 2.3, 3, 4 or 7.8 or otherwise adversely affect the holders of the Series C Preferred. 8.7 Notices. Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, courier or email to the addresses below the signatures (or another address a party gives by notice). Notice to the Company must be sent to the attention of the Chair of the Audit Committee, with a copy to Sichenzia Ross Ference Carmel LLP. 8.8 Expenses. Each party pays its own expenses. 8.9 Counterparts. This Agreement may be signed in counterparts and by electronic signature. No term is linked to the Common Stock price. Events of default Non-payment at maturity (after a 30-day cure period) and bankruptcy only; no cross-default; no acceleration or other remedy before the Series C Discharge Date Governing law Nevada [Note: the definitive form of Reinstated Note is to be agreed before the Closing in accordance with Section 4.3 .] 11 EXHIBIT B Form of Resolutions Resolutions of the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors of NextNRG, Inc. WHEREAS, Michael D. Farkas, the Company’s Chief Executive Officer, a director and a principal stockholder, holds promissory notes of NextNRG and NextNRG Holding Corp. with outstanding principal USD 3,629,924 and accrued interest of USD 2,749,169, and is owed personal guarantee fees of USD 620,907, totaling USD 7,000,000 that are proposed to be exchanged for Series D Convertible Voting Preferred Stock under a Debt Exchange Agreement (the “Agreement”); WHEREAS, the Committee consists solely of directors who are independent under Nasdaq Rule 5605(a)(2) and disinterested in the Agreement, has been informed of Mr. Farkas’s material interest in it, and has reviewed it under NRS 78.140 and Nasdaq Rule 5630; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Committee finds the Agreement fair to and in the best interests of the Company and its stockholders, approves it, and recommends that the Board adopt the Certificate of Designations of the Series D Convertible Voting Preferred Stock; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Company’s right to effect a Reconversion under the Agreement may be exercised only by resolution of this Committee (or its successor composed of independent and disinterested directors), and Mr. Farkas will not participate in any such decision; and RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Committee has confirmed that the Conversion Price of $2.20 is not less than the greater of the consolidated closing bid price of the Common Stock and the Minimum Price under Nasdaq Rule 5635(d), each measured immediately prior to the date of the Agreement, and that the voting rights of the Series D Preferred are intended to comply with Nasdaq Rule 5640, subject to the limitations in Section 6(g) of the Certificate of Designations; RESOLVED FURTHER, that Joel Kleiner, as an officer of the Company other than Mr. Farkas, is authorized to sign the Agreement and take all actions needed to complete it, including seeking the consent of the holders of the Series C Convertible Preferred Stock. Resolutions of the Board of Directors (Mr. Farkas abstaining) will designate the Series D Convertible Voting Preferred Stock under the Board’s blank-check authority in the Articles of Incorporation and NRS 78.1955, approve the Certificate of Designations and authorize its filing with the Nevada Secretary of State, and reserve [●] shares (not less than the number required by Section 6(f)(iii) of the Certificate of Designations, subject to the priority of the Series C Reserved Shares under Section 4A(c) thereof, to be determined at signing based on the Conversion Price) of Common Stock for issuance on conversion. 12 EXHIBIT C Form of Certificate of Designations [Attached: Certificate of Designations of Preferences and Rights of Series D Convertible Voting Preferred Stock, in the form attached as Exhibit A to the Series C Consent.] 13

text: EX-10.2 4 ex10-2.htm EX-10.2 Exhibit 10.2 LIMITED CONSENT AND WAIVER THIS LIMITED CONSENT AND WAIVER (this “ Waiver ”), dated as of November 2, 2026, is made by and among NextNRG, Inc., a Nevada corporation (the “ Company ”), and each of the investors listed on the signature page hereto (individually, a “ Buyer ” and collectively, the “ Buyers ”). WHEREAS , on August 13, 2026, the Company and the Buyers entered into that certain Securities Purchase Agreement (the “ Initial Securities Purchase Agreement ”), which was amended as of September 30, 2026 (the “ SPA Amendment ” and together with the Initial Securities Purchase Agreement, the “ Securities Purchase Agreement ”), pursuant to which, among other things, the Company agreed to issue and sell, and the Buyers agreed to purchase, in one or more closings shares of Series C Preferred Stock (as defined therein), the terms of which are set forth in the Certificate of Designation of Preferences, Rights and Limitations of Series C Convertible Non-Voting Preferred Stock of the Company filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Nevada on October 7, 2026 (the “ Certificate of Designation ”); all capitalized terms used, but not otherwise defined, herein shall have the respective meanings set forth in the Certificate of Designation ; WHEREAS , the Company, NextNRG Holding Corp (the “ Subsidiary ”) and Michael D. Farkas (the “ Exchange Debt Holder ”) propose to enter into an exchange agreement, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A (the “ Exchange Agreement ”), pursuant to which the Exchange Debt Holder will agree to exchange certain Indebtedness and other obligations of Company and the Subsidiary in an aggregate amount of $7.0 million (the “ Exchange Obligations ”) for 7,000 shares (the “ Exchange Shares ”) of a new series of Preferred Stock to be known as the Series D Convertible Voting Preferred Stock (the “ Series D Preferred Stock ”), which Series D Preferred Stock will be convertible into shares of Common Stock pursuant to the terms of the Certificate of Designations of Preferences and Rights of Series D Convertible Voting Preferred Stock, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit B (the “ Series D Certificate ”), which Series D Preferred Stock shall rank junior to the Series C Preferred Stock in all respects (such exchange and issuance, the “ Debt Exchange ”); WHEREAS , the Buyers desire to consent to the Debt Exchange and waive certain provisions of the Securities Purchase Agreement and the Certificate of Designation as set forth herein; and NOW, THEREFORE , in consideration of such consent and waivers and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt of which is hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto hereby agree as follows: 1. Each Buyer hereby agrees that any redemption or other such rights in connection with a Liquidation as set forth in Section 5 ( Liquidation ) of the Certificate of Designation shall apply with regard to (i) a Liquidation of the Company, and (ii) whether in a single transaction or a series of transactions, the voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up of any Subsidiary or Subsidiaries the assets of which constitute all or substantially all of the assets of the business of the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole (the proceeds of which that are available for distribution to the Company’s stockholders the Company shall cause to be distributed to the Holders in accordance with Section 5 of the Certificate of Designation), and each Buyer hereby irrevocably waives compliance with Section 5 of the Certificate of Designation solely with respect to the liquidation, dissolution or winding up of any other Subsidiary. 2. Each Buyer and the Company hereby irrevocably agree that: a.
